Self seeps into the community.

[nishio.icon] What kind of discussions have there been in the past about how [boundary between oneself and others] is not only the boundary of [individual], but also a [holon]-like [overlapping set] that [considers a social group to be the self]?

[GPT5.icon]Briefly, "[Boundaries of the self]" are discussed in many fields as multi-layered "[overlapping]" not only individuals, but also relationships, groups, institutions, and ecosystems. We will quickly map just the major genealogies.
Systems theory/Holon

[Arthur Koestler] proposed "holon" and "[holarchy]" as "something that is both whole and part. Later [Ken Wilber] extended the theory to the social and cultural level. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holon_%28philosophy%29?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Social psychology: individual ⇄ relationship ⇄ group variable self

IOS scale ([Inclusion of Other in the Self]), which measures the overlap between others and oneself in terms of overlapping circles. There is also a group version (IIS), which measures the degree of "inclusion of the inner group within oneself". ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8168758/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Social identity theory/self-categorization theory: [self-representation] switches to "[I→we]" depending on the situation, and [the group becomes "self"]. ([SAGE Knowledge https://sk.sagepub.com/ency/edvol/processes/chpt/social-identity-theory?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

[Social Identity Complexity]: the integration of multiple group affiliations into the self as "overlap". ([SAGE Journals https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1207/s15327957pspr0602_01?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

[Identity Fusion]: intense unification where the boundaries between self and group nearly dissolve. ([UT Psychology Lab https://labs.la.utexas.edu/swann/files/2016/03/Gomez-et-al-2011_JPSP.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Anthropology: [divisible] (divisible) personality
[dividual] /  [offshoot (plants; often the of grass family)] [nishio.icon]

Marilyn Strathern and Marriott present the "individual/partible person" concept, which views the person as an allocation of relationships. The individual is "allocated" to others and to the group from the beginning. ([Pirate Care Syllabus https://syllabus.pirate.care/_preview/library/Marilyn%20Strathern/The%20gender%20of%20the%20gift_%20problems% 20with%20women%20and%20problems%20with%20society%20in%20Melanesia%20%20%28468%29/The%20gender%20of%20the%20gift_%20problems%20with%20 wome%20-%20Marilyn%20Strathern.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Japanese Philosophy and Ethics: [The self as 〈in-between〉].
[Watsuji Tetsuro]'s "[aida-gara]" captures human existence as a relationship that precedes the dichotomy between the individual and society.

Kitaro Nishida's "[Location] (basho)" locates the self in a "place" that transcends subject-object separation. ([Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/japanese-philosophy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Sociological Classics
[Mead]'s "[generalized other]" is the idea that [communal attitudes give] the unity of the self.

The [collective consciousness] of [Durkheim] is a shared norm that binds its members from within. ([Brock University https://brocku.ca/MeadProject/Mead/pubs2/mindself/Mead_1934_20.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Social Philosophy/Law: Collective Intentionality and Group Agency

[Collective intentionality] ([shared intention], belief) and the argument that "[a] group can be its own agent" by [decision design] (List & Pettit). The legal doctrine of juridical personality is also historically grounded. ([Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/collective-intentionality/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Cognitive Science: Expanding and Distributed Mind

[Distributed cognition (human + tools + others as one cognitive system) and Extended Mind (mind "outside" tools and environment). Boundaries go outside the skin. ([MIT Press https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262581462/cognition-in-the-wild/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
The context in which I originally started thinking about this was[「自分」が「自分の周囲のコミュニティ」にはみ出す]と表現するのがしっくりくるものだった[nishio.icon]
Made brief: "Self seeps into the community."
[self] [seeps] into [Community]
Biology: Holobiont (host + symbiotic microorganism)

In immunology and evolution, the view that "individual = community (holobiont)" has become common due to hologenome theory and other factors. The boundary of an individual is defined by a symbiotic system. ([BioMed Central https://microbiomejournal.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s40168-018-0457-9?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Political Thought: Imagined Communities

[Anderson] describes the nation-state as an "Imaginary Community" sustained by the imagination of its members. A classic that shows the conditions under which a huge group becomes a "we. ([Encyclopedia Britannica https://www.britannica.com/topic/Imagined-Communities-Reflections-on-the-Origins-and-Spread-of-Nationalism utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Typical example of a direct hit on "overlap."
IOS/IIS overlap circle = subjective weighing of "overlap of self and others". ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8168758/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Social Identity Complexity = Structuring overlapping affiliations. ([SAGE Journals https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1207/s15327957pspr0602_01?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Identity Fusion = dissolution of boundaries (extreme overlap). ([UT Psychology Lab https://labs.la.utexas.edu/swann/files/2016/03/Gomez-et-al-2011_JPSP.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

holon / holarchy, inclusion of other/ingroup in the self (IOS/IIS), social identity complexity, identity fusion, collective intentionality / group agency, distributed cognition / extended mind, holobiont / hologenome, Watsuji “aidagara”, Nishida “basho”, imagined communities.

Gaussian regression
[nishio.icon]
[$ \mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}] function is learned to output an estimate of the outcome and its uncertainty for unknown inputs
[GPT5.icon]
Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) very roughly:
What do you do?

The relationship (f(x)) between input (x) and output (y) is learned by placing a probability (distribution) on the function itself. Predicting simultaneously produces a value (mean) and an uncertainty (variance).
Intuition (even if)

When a "soft board" is pinged at an observation point (data), the board deflects along its value near the pin and tries to return to its original level when it moves away. The closer the location, the greater the confidence; the farther away, the smaller the confidence.
The kernel (similarity) is a mathematical expression of this.
How it works (3 steps)
1. choose a kernel (k(x,x')) (RBF/Matérn/linear, etc...) (Specify the degree of "like input, like output" and smoothness).
2. insert an observation ((X,y)) and for any (x_), compute **predicted mean (\mu(x_))** and uncertainty (\sigma(x_*))
Kernel parameters (length scale, noise, etc.) are automatically adjusted from the data (maximize marginal likelihood).
What makes you happy?
Strong/uncertainty for small data, directly related to search and utilization ([UCB], [Thompson]). Useful for spatial interpolation (kriging), time series, preference estimation, etc.
Limitations / Caution

Computational complexity is (O(n^3)) (number of data (n)). For large scale, use approximation (induced points, random features = RFF, divide and conquer). Kernel selection determines performance, and extrapolation is not good.
Formula version (may be skipped)
Prior: ([$ f \sim \mathrm{GP}(m,k)]), Observation: ([$ y=f(X)+\varepsilon,\varepsilon\sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2I)]).
Prediction point (x_):
[$ \mu = k_*^\top (K+\sigma^2 I)^{-1} y]

[idobata-keichobot conversation log 2025-10-08]
[GPT5.icon]
Case Analysis from the Gendlin Perspective (Focusing Perspective)
summary

This dialogue is able to handle the client's words with clean-language-style repetitive questions, but does not fully access the felt sense of the body (vague but holistic) that is at the core of Gendlin's Focusing. As a result, the tension of "I have to do it" is returning to the thought process of "clarify how to do it," and I have the impression that the felt shift (one step lighter change at the body level) has not fully occurred.
[somesthesis] が弱いね、確かに[nishio.icon]
What works well
Reflection of client language: metaphors (i.e., candidate handles) such as "wall," "engine," "drive force," and "energy" came naturally.
Clarification of the action subject: The value of wanting to make decisions on one's own/not being easily burned by tasks given from the outside was expressed.
Visualization of the process: the choice of parallel projects was symbolized as a "barrier to progress".
stumbling
Lack of guidance to the body: "Where is it?" What kind?" are more likely to lean toward conceptual definitions, and **checking with the body (resonance)** is less likely to occur.
Lack of pacing: there is no margin for pause and silence, and time is not taken to listen inwardly.
Handling the "I don't know": "What do you think?" and reinforced the "it should be solved" argument.
I thought this.[nishio.icon]
I'm biased to only ask questions about the last statement, and I'm not grasping what's still not clear.
Quickness of Targeting: Early return to the problem-solution loop of "identify the solution". Lack of support to stay on the edge (borderline between know/not know).
If you want to do it in a focusing way (short protocol: walking version 5-7 minutes)
1. place attention on the soles of the feet and breathing
One deep breath in step. Make the "here and now" in your body.
2. feel the whole

Search for the "overall feeling of 'I must do it'" with the body (chest, throat, abdomen, shoulders, etc.). Do not try to put it into words, but capture it in terms of texture (heaviness/rushes/pressure/temperature).
3. find the handle
Try to guess the perfect word/image that fits the whole now (e.g., "wall," "blockage," "fog"). Check the fit with your body (resonance).
4. ask at the edge
What is the smallest thing this wall wants from me right now?
Wait for a small "thump" to come from the body (a physical step that can be done in 10 minutes is preferable).
5. receive
Felt shift if there is a slight change (breathing passes/strength is lost, etc.). Respect and note the step that came out.
Examples of question substitution that make use of metaphors
×x "Where is it?"
→ "Where on your body do you feel it most?" (If not, "What texture as a whole?")
×x "What type of drive force?"
→ How does your body react when you get one step closer to that "engine/wall"?
×x "If you could do that, what would you do?"
→ What is the smallest step your body says you need to take now for the "wall" to soften a bit?
Resonance check: "Does that word (e.g., 'easy to break') fit when you apply it to your body/is it any different?"
Using Focusing to Select Parallel Projects (10 minute algorithm)
1. call to mind (in order) up to three candidate project names.
2. observe the body's response to each project name (breathing/shoulders/looseness/clogging in the groin).
3.**Select the one that is the most "breathable/lightest "**.
4. ask the body for the **"next step (10 minutes)** of the project (e.g., inventory one item on the list, open the relevant folder, ping the person in charge with one line, etc.).
5. commit to perform (timer 10 minutes). When you finish, check the degree of fit with your body again.
Operational checklist on the therapist's side
□ Observe the rhythm of reflection → silence → return to the body
Why? From ** "What is the body now?" **
□ Respect "I don't know" (= sign that you have reached the edge)
→Let's feel the whole "unknowability" together.
□ Welcome a step too small (carry forward rather than cognitive resolution)
Improvement Dialog (short example)
Visitor: "A wall is standing in my way."
Supporter: "Let's see how the whole "wall" feels with your body now. ...... (wait a little). Where do you feel it the most?"
Visitor: "My chest area is hard."
Supporter: "Is 'wall' the right word for that firmness, or is it a little different?"
Interviewee: "'thick board' is closer."
Supporter: "Ask your ...... body what one step you can take in 10 minutes that is needed now for a "thicker board."
Visitor: "Don't list all the projects, just open one memo on Project A first."
Supporter: "So what happens to the firmness of the chest at one level?"
summary
Currently, it is easy to return to thinking with repetitive meta-questions, and the flow of felt sense to felt shift is weak.

Metaphors ([wall] / [engine] / [energy]) are good handles. Between the confirmation of resonance with the body and the receipt of the smallest step, it is easy for a natural focus - carry forward to advance to occur.
Next time you try "Walking Focusing 5 minutes" + "1 action for 10 minutes", you can expect a qualitative shift from **"I have to" to "I can "**.

uncommon ground
[GPT5.icon]
What does [Audrey Tang] mean by "uncommon ground" (based on actual statements)?
in a word

Tang repeatedly talks about this as a key concept for implementing plurality. Tang repeatedly talks about this as a key concept for implementation. ([rightlivelihood.org https://rightlivelihood.org/the-change-makers/find-a-laureate/audrey-tang/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Statement by Tang himself (short excerpt)

Technology allows us to find our "uncommon ground" (points of agreement that are rarely shared). This is said in the context of "being able to create policies and norms together from there." ([rightlivelihood.org https://rightlivelihood.org/the-change-makers/find-a-laureate/audrey-tang/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
The "uncommon ground" (of the public hearing and AI) will be uncovered and connected from people's different ideas. ([SayIt https://sayit.archive.tw/speech/622917?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

"Bridging Bonus algorithm increases visibility of "bridging statements" and extends bridges of agreement without inciting division by designing no reply button." ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/11310?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
"[Polis] is a tool for finding uncommon ground." ([LessWrong https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/anoK4akwe8PKjtzkL/plurality-and-6pack-care?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

He also mentioned a specific example of a misinformation countermeasure: "We found UNCOMMON ground, so we were able to quickly pre-bank messages. ([yaschamounk.substack.com https://yaschamounk.substack.com/p/audrey-tang-on-misinformation?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

By designing the right "place" and making **uncommon points of agreement** visible, the energy of conflict can be transformed into the energy of co-creation" ([MediaConnect ]). ([MediaConnect https://mediaconnect.com/audrey-tang-tokyos-role-in-a-world-of-rapid-change?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
How it works (summary)

1. broad listening: Collect opinions from a large group of people through Polis and other means. Avoid designing "punching each other" with replies and quotes, and focus on voting for and against and summarizing. ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/11310?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

2. bridging emphasis: a design that rewards bridging, i.e., floating bridging statements that attract support from both different opinion groups to the top of the list. ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/11310?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

(3) Consensus foundation → Practice: Based on the visualized "uncommon ground", connect to stakeholder meetings and regulatory design. ([Northwest Asian Weekly https://nwasianweekly.com/2025/02/taiwans-audrey-tang-shares-views-on-healthy-open-source-pro-social-ai/?utm _source=chatgpt.com])
representative example
Uber Regulation (vTaiwan)

It was stated that the policy is to organize the issues in Polis of thousands of people and reflect the agreed items in the new rules (including responses to "coherent blended volition"). ([info.vtaiwan.tw https://info.vtaiwan.tw/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Countermeasures against misinformation (pre-banking)

The practice of finding [points of agreement that are acceptable to both sides] and getting the message out quickly to limit fragmentation. ([yaschamounk.substack.com https://yaschamounk.substack.com/p/audrey-tang-on-misinformation?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Public Space Design

Tang explained that [Designed not to let you reply] and [bridging visualization] are ideas that also run through collective knowledge tools such as Community Notes. ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/11310?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Difference from "[common ground]"
common ground = common sense assumptions that everyone originally shares.

Tang speaks of finding this in the design of tools and places as a framework for transforming fragmentation into co-creation. ([MediaConnect https://mediaconnect.com/audrey-tang-tokyos-role-in-a-world-of-rapid-change?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Points that are often misunderstood

This is not **moderation (taking the middle ground)**. The key point is that it "amplifies by design" claims that really overlap among different tribes. ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/11310?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Nor is it "AI decides." It is collective knowledge support to help humans build consensus. ([rebootdemocracy.ai https://rebootdemocracy.ai/blog/audrey-tang-ai-democracy?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
To dig even deeper.
Numerous references to "uncommon ground" in Tang's speech transcripts (SayIt): 2025-08-05 speech, 2025-09-25 speech, etc. ([SayIt https://sayit.archive.tw/speech/622917?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

The core of the concept is also discussed in the introduction to **Plurality (co-authored)** and on the awards page. ([rightlivelihood.org https://rightlivelihood.org/the-change-makers/find-a-laureate/audrey-tang/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

3-1. digital democracy "boom" or river?
In response to the title "Reflections on the Digital Democracy Boom," Nishio is uncomfortable:
Boom = nuance of temporary fad
In fact, the river of democracy is changing its course as new waters of print, broadcasting, Internet, and AI flow into it.
Can we justify majority rule in a world where AI is smarter than the average human?
→ If this trend continues, future historians may describe the idea of democracy as a "boom that lasted for hundreds of years"....
Digital democracy is the search for "something better" in the middle of traditional democracy vs. leaving everything to AI.
3-2. polis / sunflower movement / vTaiwan to Japan
Birth of Polis:
Social networking was used to mobilize during the Arab Spring, but not to deliberate or build consensus.
→ From there Polis was born (2012)
2014 Taiwan Sunflower Student Movement:
Students Occupy Parliament for 24 Days
g0v's CPR team & Audrey's onsite network
Live Broadcast Turns "Rioter" Framing on its Head
Then connect to vTaiwan, Talk to the City in Tokyo, Bowling Green 2050, Hirohari AI, etc.
The genealogy that Mr. Nishio drew on his slides:
Arab Spring → Polis → Sunflower Movement → vTaiwan → Talk to the City → Wide Hearing AI → Future Broad Listening
3-3. the crisis of democracy and the position of Japan
Ken Suzuki part:
Stop the Steal" in the U.S. → Occupy Congress
Barbara Walter's model of civil war: "Half-baked democracy" has high risk of civil war.
Democracy Index: rose after the Cold War, but began to decline in the last decade to end-Cold War levels.
Democracy defense is becoming increasingly difficult as we are entering the "New Cold War" phase starting in 2021
Japan can be the "last bastion of democracy" / If we don't stop it here, it will be tough worldwide.
Japan could become a fully-fledged divided society in 5-10 years, and we need to rebuild democracy now.
3-4. hurdles to participation, awareness of parties, accessibility
Do we need party consciousness in a digital democracy?" The question:
Nishio's answer:
Many people have already written their opinions on Twitter.
The problem is "not reaching the government side" and "not being structured"
That's where tools like Polis and broadband AI are needed.
How do we engage people who are not good at digital?
Instead of a "digitally strong vs. digitally weak" divide, technology can be used to save the non-digital segment of the population through voice → transcription → analysis, etc.
Currently, text input is a hurdle, but expects to be voice and conversational based in a few years.
3-5. the indicator/KPI trap
Is the "consensus rate" really appropriate as an indicator for evaluating the consensus building process? Is it really appropriate as an indicator of the consensus building process?
Brainwashing will increase the agreement rate.
→ Be careful what you maximize when establishing KPIs
Final indicators include citizens' life satisfaction, but the quality of consensus building and final outcomes are different.

Short answer: g0v started creating a "shadow government" site by replacing .gov.tw → .g0v.tw at the end of 2012 -- especially in October-December 2012. In particular, the starting point was the movement from October to December 2012. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G0v_movement])
Mini-timeline (why, when, how it started)

The official website of the Ministry of the Interior's "Jikkai Tengruko" became unstable shortly after its release. Volunteer engineers create their own map of real prices (crawl public data and visualize the map). Here, the idea of "parallel implementation of public services by citizens" sprouts. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G0v_movement])
10/19/2012 Before and after

The government's "Economic Dynamics Promotion Plan" ad is controversial because it is a "trust me, it's complicated" type of ad. Inspired by this, four hackers at [Yahoo! Open Hack Day 2012] hastily created and won an award for a visualization of the central government's total budget (Budget Maps); CL Kao registered g0.v.tw as a domain "for remixing government sites by citizens. v.tw as a "domain for remixing government sites by citizens. Since then, citizen versions of official sites, such as lvr.land.moi.g0v.tw / budget.g0v.tw, have been released one after another, with "one letter difference" from official sites. This is the beginning of what is commonly referred to as "unauthorized forking. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G0v_movement])

The "Zeroth (Hackath0n)" was held. Since then, the bimonthly large-scale hackathons have taken root, and a culture has spread that "if you replace .gov with .g0v, you can go to the shadow government site". ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G0v_movement])

**Permanent projects, such as the Legislative Council Portal (ly.g0v.tw), are launched, and the "parallel implementation -> improvement proposals (fork -> merge)** kineticism is solidified, including cross-search and comparison of bills and proceedings, and visualization of voting results. ([g0v.github.io https://g0v.github.io/g0v.us/tw/])
Since 2014 (Sunflower Movement)

The g0v style results are being "incorporated" into the government side of things. **The explanation that "replacing O with 0 is a shadow government "** was repeatedly given in lectures by Audrey Tang and others, and the path of "unauthorized parallel implementation" at first, followed by "public-private merger "** has taken root. and then a "public-private confluence "**. ([SayIt https://sayit.pdis.nat.gov.tw/speech/100031?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Key Points (Organizing the Historical Process)
Motivation: "Re-implementation from the citizen side" in response to the failure of government information presentation and e-governance. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G0v_movement])

Method: Instead of "hacking" to alter the official site, citizens build their own "shadow version" on a separate domain based on public information (avoiding legal risks and ensuring criticality). The watchword is fork → merge back (if you like) ([g0v.github.io https://g0v.github.io/g0v.us/tw/])

Turning point: award funding at the end of 2012 established a hackathon culture and mass production of .g0v parallel implementations at once; spilled over into the policy formation process (vTaiwan, etc.) from 2014 onward. ([g0v.github.io https://g0v.github.io/g0v.us/tw/])

[nishio.icon]Instead of having Polis-like data on each individual's vote and calculating the correlation, summarize it as data on the percentage of agreement or disagreement for each individual question and use it as a one-dimensional measure of more or less agreement?
[gpt5.icon]Yes, that understanding is almost OK.

Sensemaker does not create correlations or clusters (Polis Opinion Groups type) based on individual x statement voting vectors, but only on the aggregate ratio of agree/disagree/pass for each statement to select statements suitable for "Common Ground/Differences of Opinion". The small sample is used to avoid misinterpretation. Small samples are excluded if the total number of votes is less than 20 to avoid misinterpretation. The text is used only for "topic selection and assignment" and not for the agreement/difference selection itself.

In addition, Relative Agreement is calculated by comparing "the number of statements in the Common Ground/the total number of statements in that subtopic" in each subtopic relative to other subtopics and assigning a High/Low value to each subtopic. --In other words, here again, it is treated as a one-dimensional "strength of agreement" indicator.

You will group the claims (CLAIMS) so that users can understand "which themes are most important" in this consultation. The goal is to merge similar claims into a supportive grouping, while retaining a truly unique perspective.

Grouping Decision Framework (FRAMEWORK):.
Step 1 - Identification of core themes:.
Ask yourself: "What are the "three to five main ideas or concerns" that are commonly expressed in all these claims?"
These are the candidate groups.
Step 2 - Apply grouping criteria:.
Combine claims into the same group if they share any of the following: 1.
✓ Same underlying concern/problem (even if proposed solutions are different)
✓ Identical recommendations/solutions (even if differently reasoned)
✓ Same values and principles expressed
✓ Different aspects of the same topic (e.g., "high cost" + "unclear price" = price concerns)
✓ Specific examples of common patterns
Claims will remain in a separate group only if: - The claim is made by the same person.
✗ We are dealing with a completely different topic within this subtopic.
✗ Opposing positions (for or against something) are expressed.
✗ One is about process/method (how) and the other is about outcome/what (what)
Step 3 - Creating a Strong Group Claim: The group claim must be a strong group claim.
For each group, write a claim that satisfies the following
- Capture the shared essence at a higher level of abstraction
- Use vocabulary and concepts that appear in the original claim (avoid introducing new terms)
- Level of specificity and meaning (avoid vague common phrases such as "improve X")
- All citations in the group could reasonably support
- Clear and plain language
- Be faithful to what the participants say
Step 4 - Group validation:.
- Prioritize natural thematic consistency over meeting target group numbers
- Each group should represent a clear and meaningful theme
- Groups with only a single claim should be relatively rare. If there are many, reexamine to see if you have overlooked any superordinate themes that link the claims together.
- Avoid excessive consolidation: don't force merging to reduce numbers.
- The appropriate number of groups depends on the natural diversity of viewpoints in the input

- "It's hard to understand how the parking pass works."

Epistemic Security
[GPT5.icon]
[Epistemic Security]
[cognitive security].
summary

Definition (closer to practice): the state/ability of a democratic society to continuously avoid factors that threaten the process of producing, distributing, acquiring, and evaluating reliable knowledge. The Turning Institute report formulates this as a challenge to the "resilience of the social epistemic infrastructures" of society. ([turing.ac.uk https://www.turing.ac.uk/news/publications/tackling-threats-informed-decision-making-democratic-societies?utm_source =chatgpt.com])

Positioning in policy context: The UK think tank Demos summarizes that at the national level it is "about ensuring the health of the information supply chains" (the report positions the term as having been coined by researchers at DSTL, Cambridge University, and the Turning Laboratory in 2020). (The report positions that this term was organized by the DSTL, University of Cambridge, and the Turning Institute in 2020). ([Demos https://demos.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Epistemic-Security-2029_accessible.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
What threatens the "knowledge security" of society (typical example)?

Systematic disinformation/manipulation of information, de-authorization of specialized knowledge, growing distrust of knowledge production and distribution institutions, extreme fragmentation, censorship, suppression of diverse perspectives, abuse of generative AI and persuasive AI, etc. ([Elizabeth Seger https://elizabethseger.com/epistemic-security/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Relationship to Audrey Tang (Tang Feng) (as confirmed by primary sources)

Tang referred to "human attention and epistemic security" as one of the pillars of AI research in the dialogue transcript ("human attention and epistemic security"). The term is used directly. ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/8765?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

He also reiterated that the reduction of "epistemic injustice" ([epistemic injustice]) will be incorporated into the government's AI evaluation framework (AI evaluation centers to inspect AI for fictionalization and epistemic injustice). This is an example of implementation of institutional preservation of "knowledge security". ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/9411?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
As a practical operation, it was established in Taiwan.

"[humor over rumor] (2-2-2)": a 20-minute, 200-word, 2-image quick response operation to "happily" counteract the rumor. ([Guardian https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2021/feb/17/humour-over-rumour-taiwan-fake-news?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Cofacts: citizen-driven, open-source fact-checking infrastructure (messaging-driven verification community). ([Cornell Tech https://tech.cornell.edu/news/crowdsourced-fact-checking-fights-misinformation-in-taiwan/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

vTaiwan/Polis: Visualizing "rough consensus" for each issue and strengthening the foundation for consensus building (i.e., social cognitive infrastructure). ([blog.pol.is https://blog.pol.is/uber-responds-to-vtaiwans-coherent-blended-volition-3e9b75102b9b?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Difference from "Cognitive Security" (key points of confusion)

Cognitive Security: A defense concept (developed by NATO and others) that protects the realm of the mind against attacks and influence operations that target a person's cognition itself (attention, judgment, and behavior). ([NATO https://www.nato.int/docu/review/articles/2021/05/20/countering-cognitive-warfare-awareness-and-resilience/index.html?utm_ source=chatgpt.com])

Epistemic Security: the concept of making the social processes by which knowledge is established and shared (observation → verification → distribution → evaluation → decision making) robust at the institutional, community, and information supply network levels. ([turing.ac.uk https://www.turing.ac.uk/news/publications/tackling-threats-informed-decision-making-democratic-societies?utm_source =chatgpt.com])
Ready-to-use operational checklist (short version)

1. information supply network KPIs: speed of primary information release, time-to-revision (TTR) to correction, reproducibility across media. ([Demos https://demos.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Epistemic-Security-2029_accessible.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

2. social cognitive infrastructure: constantly monitor participation base and disprovability of fact-checking (e.g. Cofacts) and consensus indicators in discussion space (e.g. Polis). ([Cornell Tech https://tech.cornell.edu/news/crowdsourced-fact-checking-fights-misinformation-in-taiwan/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

3. pre-banking: convergence before diffusion with a preemptive narrative design such as the 2-2-2 operation. ([Guardian https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2021/feb/17/humour-over-rumour-taiwan-fake-news?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

4. AI evaluation: introduce inspection indicators of illusions/biases/cognitive unfairness and create a cycle of disclosure and improvement. ([moda.gov.tw https://moda.gov.tw/en/press/background-information/9411?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

[Open question - Wikipedia https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%AA%E3%83%BC%E3%83%97%E3%83%B3%E3%82%AF%E3%82%A8%E3%82%B9%E3%83%81%E3%83% A7%E3%83%B3]

>In educational settings, [open questions] are generally considered "good" questions. Open questions result in longer responses that allow students to demonstrate their understanding. Open questions are considered preferable to closed questions in this regard because they are more appropriate for discussion and exploration, whereas closed questions (questions that require a "yes"/"no" response) are only appropriate for testing.

> [Peter Worley] argues that this is a false assumption. This is based on Worley's central argument that there are two different kinds of open and closed questions: grammatical and conceptual. He argues that educators should aim for questions that are "grammatically closed but conceptually open." For example, in standard parlance, "Is it right to lie?" would be considered a closed question. However, what is important is that it is conceptually open. The initial "yes"/"no" answer to this question is the questioner's "Why do you think so?" "Could it be otherwise?" can be made "open" by the questioner's "Why do you think so?" and "Could it be otherwise?" which can encourage detailed explanation and exploration.

> This grammatically closed but conceptually open question style offers educators the best of both worlds. It combines the "focus" and "specificity" of closed questions (which is, after all, why teachers use closed questions) with the dual benefits of "invitation" and "detail" of open questions, Worley argues. Closed questions simply require a strategy for "opening up" in order to ensure that conceptually open questions can fulfill their pedagogical potential.

> Worley's structural and semantic differences between open-ended and closed questions are integral to his educational invention, "[the] Open Questioning Mindset (OQM)," which refers to educators developing an open attitude toward the learning process and the questions at its heart. It is a concept that can be applied to all subjects and all educational environments. Teachers who develop an open questioning mindset listen openly to the cognitive content of student statements and look for ways to use what is given as an opportunity for learning, regardless of whether it is right or wrong, or appears to be relevant or irrelevant. oQM encourages a teaching style that emphasizes authentic inquiry in the classroom. Encouraging a teaching style that emphasizes what Worley calls "guess what's in my head," OQM provides teachers with the tools to move beyond a closed, guided questioning approach to teaching.

Random Kitchen Sinks
[Random Features for Large-Scale Kernel Machines]（Rahimi & Recht, NIPS 2007）
Approximate the kernel with random features (e.g., random Fourier features) and accelerate with linear learning.
[PDF https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2007/file/013a006f03dbc5392effeb8f18fda755-Paper.pdf]
Sequel [Weighted Sums of Random Kitchen Sinks: Replacing Minimization with Randomization in Learning] (Rahimi & Recht, NIPS 2008/Proc. 2009)
Generalized "RKS" and analyzed as a weighted sum of random nonlinear bases.
[GPT5.icon]
Approximate what?
The original GP ([Gaussian regression]) uses [kernel] (k(x,x')) to express smoothness, where close points are predicted to be close.
However, strictly speaking GP is O(N³) (N=number of study points) and heavy.

Therefore, we create an explicit feature map ([$ \phi(x)]) that is "kernel ≈ inner product" with random features ([Random Fourier Features]; [RFF]) and perform [linear regression] (≈[Bayesian linear regression]) on it.
This is GP approximation by "random features x linear regression".
Also known as Random Kitchen Sinks.
Intuition (why does it work?)
[RBF] system kernel can be expressed by Fourier transform → Adding random waves (frequency and phase) approximates a "smooth" function space.
So if we convert "[$ \phi(x)] = vector of random waves" and learn ([$ \hat y = w^\top \phi(x)]), we can replace nonlinear regression with linear regression.
Formula (minimum set)
1) Random features (example of RBF kernel)
Randomly [$ \omega_j \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{\ell^2}I)), (b_j \sim \mathrm{Unif}[0,2\pi]]
Feature mapping (dimension D)
[$ \phi_j(x) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{D}} \cos(\omega_j^\top x + b_j), \quad j=1,\dots,D ]
Then [$ k(x,x') \approx \phi(x)^\top \phi(x')]
If the embedding is **normalized (L2=1)**, then instead of Euclidean distance
The RBF equivalent using the cosine distance ([$ 1 - x\cdot x']) is also acceptable in practice.
It is sufficient to simply follow the "random projection -> cos" for implementation.
2) Linear regression (Bayesian version = can also produce uncertainty)
Observation: ([$ y = \Phi w + \varepsilon), (\varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_n^2 I)])
where [$ \Phi ] is [$ [\phi(x_1)^\top; \dots; \phi(x_N)^\top] ]
Pre: [$ w \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\lambda^{-1} I)] (ridge regularization)
Posterior mean and variance:
[$ \Sigma = \big(\lambda I + \tfrac{1}{\sigma_n^2}\Phi^\top \Phi \big)^{-1},\qquad \mu_w = \tfrac{1}{\sigma_n^2}\Sigma \Phi^\top y ]
Predicted mean and variance (new point (x_*)):
[$ \mu(x_*) = \phi(x_*)^\top \mu_w,\quad \mathrm{Var}(x_*) \approx \phi(x_*)^\top \Sigma, \phi(x_*) + \sigma_n^2]
UCB is [$ \text{UCB}(x)=\mu(x)+\sqrt{\beta}\sigma(x)]
So far, **GP-like "average + uncertainty "** can be obtained at a low cost.
Procedure (Implementation Flow)
1. pre-processing
Text -> Embedded (e.g., 1536 dimensions)
L2 normalization (important: easy to use cosine for distance)
2. preparation of RFF (one time only)
Determine dimension D (256 to 1024 for MVP)
Fixed random numbers (\omega, b) (seed retained/not regenerated each time)
3. study set creation
Create (\Phi) from the evaluated ((x_i, y_i))
Compute (\Sigma, \mu_w) (D×D matrix inverted once)
4. inference of unrated points
Apply φ(x) to each (x) to obtain (\mu(x), \sigma(x))
Arranged in UCB order and presented in MMR to ensure diversity
5. re-study (light) when new evaluations are accumulated
Parameter Guideline
D (RFF dimension): 256 (ultralight) to 1024 (accuracy up, cost up)
(\ell) (length scale): 0.5 to 1.0 equivalent (depends on the distance of embedding)
(\lambda) (prior accuracy, ridge): from around 1.0. Raise by over-learning.
(\sigma_n) (Observation noise): around 0.2 (Measures for blurring of evaluation. Can be estimated from duplicate evaluations)
(\beta) (search degree of UCB): 1.0 to 2.0 (the larger the value, the closer to search)
What is "light" about it?
The bottleneck is the inverse (once) of D×D, O(D³).
If D=512, even JS/Deno can fit in a few hundred ms to a few seconds.
Subsequent inferences are made at each point O(D) (fast).
It is much lighter than O(N³) in strict GP.
Common Pitfalls
RFF is regenerated every time → φ does not match between learning and inference and collapses.
→ Random numbers are fixed (seed management).
Embedding is not normalized → distance scale is broken and σ is strange.
→ Ensure that L2=1.
D is too small → Bias (lack of expression).
→ Verified by increasing from 256 to 512 to 1024....
Numerical instability → (\lambda) slightly higher / double precision / small epsilon to prevent divergence.
UCBs are all similar candidates → diversity penalty in MMR (deduct the cosine maximum with the already selected).
Minimal pseudo code (TypeScript/Edge Functions style)
code:ts
// Preparation (1 time): RFF parameters
const D = 512, l = 0.7; // dimension and length scales
const W = randn(d, D, 1/(l*l));    // N(0, 1/l^2)
const b = uniform(D, 0, 2*Math.PI);
const phi = (x: number[]) => {
const u = l2norm1(x); // L2 normalization
const z = new Array(D);
for (let j=0;j<D;j++){
let s = 0; for (let i=0;i<d;i++) s += W[i][j]*u[i];
z[j] = Math.SQRT2*Math.cos(s + b[j])/Math.sqrt(D);
return z;
// Learning (each time an evaluation is accumulated)
const Phi = X_labeled.map(phi);    // N×D
const XtX = gram(Phi);             // D×D
const A   = addDiag(XtX, lambda);  // ridge
const Ainv= inv(A);
const Xty = Phi[0].map((_,j)=> dotCol(Phi,j, y)); // D×1
const w   = matvec(Ainv, Xty);
// Prediction (not yet evaluated)
for (const x of X_unlabeled) {
const p  = phi(x);
const mu = dot(w, p);
const var= quad(p, Ainv) + sigma_n*sigma_n;
const ucb= mu + Math.sqrt(beta)*Math.sqrt(var);
// → ucb order + presented in MMR
summary
RFF x linear regression is a lightweight practical approximation to the "mean and uncertainty" of GP.
Ideal for low-cost MVP as it also turns in Edge Functions (Deno/TS).
Edge Functions could be used for 500 cases, but timeout would occur for 1000 cases.[nishio.icon]
First, D=256-512, L2 normalization, fixed random numbers, UCB coefficient=1.5 is sufficient.
If it is not enough, move to D↑ or **Python worker (GPyTorch)**.

Pace Layers
[GPT5.icon]
**Pace Layers** is a concept proposed by architect and thinker [Stewart Brand] that describes the different rates of change in societies and organizational and technological systems.
🔹 Basic Ideas
The layers that make up the world (layers) change at different speeds.
The fast layer creates innovation, while the slow layer brings stability.
The idea is that this difference in speed allows for "sustainable evolution" as a whole.
🔹 Six Layers (from Stewart Brand, [The Clock of the Long Now])
table:_
Layer Speed of change Example Role
Fashion months to years Design, SNS culture, clothing Create new and tried-and-true
Commerce Several to 10 years Business model, corporate strategy Implement innovation economically
Infrastructure (infrastructure) Decades Transportation networks, telecommunications networks, power grids Stable social infrastructure
Governance Decades to centuries Legal, administrative, and educational systems Equity and long-term order
Culture Hundreds of years Customs, religion, family structure Maintain social identity and values
Nature Thousands of years - Ecosystems, geology, climate Slowest change, life base
🔹 Key Insights
The fast layer experiments and the slow layer gives stability.
Example: fashion may change politics, but culture absorbs it and nature constrains it.
The "friction" between the upper (fast) and lower (slow) layers creates healthy evolution.
This is interesting.[速さと遅さの摩擦が健全な進化を生む]」[nishio.icon]
Associated [Fast and Slow Worlds].
[Change too fast creates fragility, and change too slow creates stagnation.
When all layers function in tandem, the system is supple and sustainable.
🔹 Contemporary Applications
IT system design (e.g., Gartner's "[Pace-Layered Application Strategy]")
The application is managed by dividing it into System of Record (stable), System of Differentiation (medium speed), and System of Innovation (high speed).
Urban design and policy making
Conscious of coordinating short-term measures (politics) with long-term culture and infrastructure.
organizational change
Separate new business (high speed) from core business (low speed) and design a structure to control friction.

Digital Policy Forum Lecture 2025-11-19
Social Implementation of Digital Democracy
Where technology is now and bottlenecks
[Digital Policy Forum]
Document [Slide https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1ED6vm5bpTIBphCDtSIWmiU10WuNkx4ViZNhhOZ0aNfk/edit?slide=id.p#slide=id.p]
Lecture Contents
[GPT5.icon]
This entire slide is "Where are the bottlenecks when implementing digital democracy in society?
(1) Techniques for consensus building (2) Techniques for discovering new perspectives (broad listening)
The story is organized in two parts.
1. consensus building techniques (Aoyama Part)
problem-solving

Real-world policies can easily fall into the "complexity trap," where variables and stakeholders such as the economy, the environment, local sentiment, and future generations are intertwined and exceed human cognitive limits.
As a result, the world is simplified into "friend/foe" and the discussion does not engage.
Case 1: Taiwan Uber Regulation x Polis
There was a "governance vacuum" between the cab association, Uber, and the government, and no one could really take ownership, so there was a stalemate.
About 2,000 people spoke + voted for or against in Polis, visualizing a deep division between the two groups of "Uber oustees" and "Uber defenders".
The algorithm is designed to make participants want to write "inclusive proposals" by prominently placing "opinions that their opposing group also agrees with" in a prominent position.
As a result, instead of "Uber ban/liberalization".
The government will also introduce a rating system and other measures to the cab industry to encourage quality improvement comparable to that of Uber.
and a statement of 95% agreement.

Furthermore, this "80%+ consensus list" will directly become the agenda for the government-sponsored conference, with the Minister, Uber, and the Taxi Association committing to it in a live-streaming session, leading to specific legislative changes.
→ Keywords: Polis × online consensus building × direct link to political process
Case Study 2: Israel-Palestine x Remesh
After the war, both physical face to face and dialogue across Hebrew/Arabic are nearly impossible.
138 Israeli Jews/Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza/Palestinians of Israeli nationality at Remesh, an AI dialogue platform.
First, in the Uninational Phase, each group will verbalize their redlines and visions using AI translation and summarization, and then proceed to the Joint Phase.
AI scores statements supported by both sides in Bridging-based Ranking.
A mirror-image line was extracted: "No justification for the 10/7 attack will be tolerated," and "No justification for the war in Gaza will be tolerated,
Explanation and
Moral justification (Justification)
The AI analysis reveals that the distinction between

The Equal Power Metrics defined "tripartite consensus" rather than majority rule by using "the group with the lowest approval rating among the three groups" as the criterion. The Equal Power Metrics defines "three-way consensus" rather than majority rule by using "the least supportive of the three groups" as the standard.
Conclusions and Limitations of this Part
Technologies such as Polis and Remesh aid in sensemaking:
Rather than a simple tally, it visualizes "what are the issues and where can there be agreement" and encourages internal transformation of the participants themselves.

However, AI has a limitation (dilemma of concreteness) in that it is strong for abstract "safe and sound" agreements such as "peace is important," but weak for "painful agreements" that include border lines and concrete trade-offs. The dilemma of concreteness is a limitation.

In addition, the "connection design" (where and who intervenes and how) that connects the discussion on the citizen side and the decision-making process on the politician/administrator side is still a bottleneck.
2. the art of discovering new perspectives = broad listening (Nishio part)
Scatter Visualization is only "part of broad listening"

In the 2024 House election and other elections, Talk to the City is used to create scatter plots using a pipeline of LLM to make statements about people's opinions → embedding → UMAP → clustering → LLM to generate cluster names and explanations.
However, as emphasized in the slide,
Visualization of scatter plots of opinions does not = broad listening
Scatter plots have become famous because they stand out, but the essence is "to receive many voices and not get punked.
Value for each of the three types of stakeholders
1. citizen
If the analysis is a black box, "I wonder if the opinion has been discarded?" I feel that.
A "sense of acceptance" is created when one's opinions appear as dots on a scatterplot or when one sees the AI's summary.
2. data analyst
LLM has made "sentence → high-dimensional vector → clustering" realistic and capable of handling large amounts of free descriptions.
As a result, "the burden of summarizing what is common is reduced → more room for paying attention to minority opinions → easier to discover new viewpoints.
3. decision makers

Although UMAP/scatter plots can be used to get a rough idea of the overall picture, they tend to be misinterpreted as "big clusters are great" when in fact the smaller clusters may be "important agendas that were overlooked.
Furthermore, the LLM-ized analysis process reveals a direction to convert the decision maker's Japanese questions directly into instructions for the analysis process.
3. examples: 2050 Tokyo Strategy, BG2050, Talkable Manifesto
2050 Tokyo Strategy × Talk to the City

Nearly 30,000 opinions were collected from multiple channels, including Google Forms, X, YouTube comments, email, mail, and street interviews, and were clustered and summarized using Talk to the City.
Citizens' opinions were applied to the existing "Future Tokyo" strategy's classification items,
New items were created from opinions that did not fit into the existing classification.
Items that do not receive much input are merged.
Subdivide where the volume is large and the content is different.
The policy system is being restructured in such a way that
BG2050 (Bowling Green, Kentucky)

An online dialogue called "What Could BG Be?" was conducted for a month using Polis and Sensemaker in a city with a population of 75,000. It is said to have attracted about 8,000 participants, 3-4,000 opinions and 1 million votes.
The visualization is a bubble chart drawn by the designer, but behind the bubble chart is a two-level tree classification by Sensemaker, which was originally designed to drill down into the tree.
Talkable Manifesto (Team Mirai)

This system was used in the Upper House election. Citizens interact with AI chat, and based on the logs, the AI generates manifesto change proposals, which are reflected in manifests on GitHub in a pull-like fashion.
Of the 8,559 proposals, 254 were adopted as manifesto improvements, using broad listening as a "strategy to pick up on fairly detailed issues → deeply penetrate a small number of people.
4. what we have already done and what we aim to do in the future
What has already been done
1.(1) Analyze large numbers of natural language opinions with LLM to reduce the burden on the analyst (embedding/clustering/summarizing).
2.(2) Polis and AI Depth Interviews (talking manifesto type AI Interviews) to encourage verbalization from citizens.
3.(3) The analyst and the AI agent interact in natural language to turn the analysis process together.
What I want to do in the near future
Streamline the feedback loop between the decision maker ↔ analyst, so that the decision maker's questions can be answered directly by the AI + existing data.

Streamline the feedback loop between decision makers ↔ citizens and create a system where decision makers write in natural language "what they want to ask" and AI interviewers ask hundreds of questions and return a summary.
5. overall summary message
Broadcasting by mass media (a technique for conveying the opinions of a few to the many) already exists.
With LLM, broad listening (the art of receiving a multitude of opinions) has become a practical way to gather and make sense of a large number of citizen voices.
Tools such as Polis/Remesh/Sensemaker/Talk to the City/Hear the City/Hear the City AI/Speakable Manifesto,
Supporting consensus building
Discover new perspectives
Circulate a feedback loop between citizens, analysts, and decision makers
The overall framework of the slide is that the "interface design" that connects these pieces will become the bottleneck in the future.

embedding and kernel functions
[nishio.icon]
A [kernel function] is a generalization of the concept of [inner product
Interpreting the inner product being close to 1 in the normalized embedding vector as "close distance".
The assumption that if the distance is close, then the value of the function is also close is the "assumption about the shape of the function entered by the kernel function.
[GPT5.icon]
Conclusion: Almost correct. but in the context of the [Gaussian process] it is even more accurate with only two points of reinforcement.
1) Kernel = "[covariance function]" as well as "generalized inner product"
In GP, [$ k(x,x')=\mathrm{cov}(f(x),f(x'))] is designed directly.

The understanding that it is a generalization of the inner product is the correct entry point, but it is good to emphasize that it is a prior (PRIOR) blueprint that even determines "what functions are likely to appear (smoothness and behavior)".

For distance-dependent (equilibrium/isotropic) kernels such as [RBF]/[Matérn], the assumption is that "the distance is close ⇒ the function value is also close," but there are kernels such as linear, polynomial, periodic, and spectral mixtures that are not distance-dependent.
2) "inner product close to 1 in normalized embedding = close distance"
This is strictly OK; for a vector of unit length
So it is equivalent to "inner product is large = Euclidean distance is small" (also consistent with the user's confirmed assumption).
For embedding: practical kernel candidates
Cosine/Linear (normalized to unit length, linear kernel [$ k(x,x')=x\cdot x'])
Simple and fast. Correlation is linear (weak smoothness assumption).
RBF (angular distance version in unit ball)
[$ k(x,x')=\sigma^2 \exp \Big(-\tfrac{|x-x'|^2}{2\ell^2}\Big) =\sigma^2 \exp\Big(-\tfrac{1-x \cdot x'}{\ell^2}\Big) ]

[Gaussian Process Optimization in the Bandit Setting: No Regret and Experimental Design]

>Many applications require optimizing an unknown, noisy function that is expensive to evaluate. We formalize this task as a multi-armed bandit problem, where the payoff function is either sampled from a [Gaussian process] (GP) or has low RKHS norm. We resolve the important open problem of deriving regret bounds for this setting, which imply novel convergence rates for GP optimization. We analyze [GP-UCB], an intuitive upper-confidence based algorithm, and bound its cumulative regret in terms of maximal information gain, establishing a novel connection between GP optimization and experimental design. Moreover, by bounding the latter in terms of operator spectra, we obtain explicit sublinear regret bounds for many commonly used covariance functions. In some important cases, our bounds have surprisingly weak dependence on the dimensionality. In our experiments on real sensor data, GP-UCB compares favorably with other heuristical GP optimization approaches.
https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.3995
[Randomized Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound with Tighter Bayesian Regret Bounds]

>Gaussian process upper confidence bound ([GP-UCB]) is a theoretically promising approach for black-box optimization; however, the confidence parameter β is considerably large in the theorem and chosen heuristically in practice. Then, randomized GP-UCB (RGP-UCB) uses a randomized confidence parameter, which follows the Gamma distribution, to mitigate the impact of manually specifying β. This study first generalizes the regret analysis of RGP-UCB to a wider class of distributions, including the Gamma distribution. Furthermore, we propose improved RGP-UCB (IRGP-UCB) based on a two-parameter exponential distribution, which achieves tighter Bayesian regret bounds. IRGP-UCB does not require an increase in the confidence parameter in terms of the number of iterations, which avoids over-exploration in the later iterations. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of IRGP-UCB through extensive experiments.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.01511

pages.title: Mapping LLM Tools for Public Discourse, Pluralism & Social Cohesion

lines.text: Mapping LLM Tools for Public Discourse, Pluralism & Social Cohesion
[PDF https://techandsocialcohesion.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Mapping-LLMs-Tools-for-Public-Discourse-Pluralism-Social-Cohesion.pdf]
[GPT5.icon]

[Based on a meeting of over 70 stakeholders in early 2025, a number of real projects were organized and an overarching frame and case studies were presented. Based on a meeting of over 70 stakeholders in early 2025, a number of actual projects are organized and an overarching frame of reference and examples are presented. ([Prosocial Design Network https://www.prosocialdesign.org/blog/report-mapping-llm-tools-for-public-discourse-pluralism-social-cohesion])
Axis of mapping (3x3x4 idea)
(1) Timing: Before/During/After (self-reflection before speaking, mediation during dialogue, and reflection and consensus extraction after the dialogue is over)
(2) Scale: Individual/Group/System (Individual, Small Group, Institution)

Intent: Welcome/Connect/Inform/Empower (welcome participation/bridge/support with context and validation/connect to decision-making) - not censorship or one-size-fits-all "correction" but reflection and relationship design. A perspective that designs reflection and relationships, rather than censorship or one-size-fits-all "correction. ([techandsocialcohesion.substack.com https://techandsocialcohesion.substack.com/p/heres-how-ai-makes-online-conversations?utm_ source=chatgpt.com])
Positioning of representative tools (systems mentioned in the article)

Individual x Before (self-reflective nudge): CLR:SKY (visualizes tone when drafting Bluesky. (Visualize the tone when drafting Bluesky and encourage "self-correction") ([CLR:SKY - Civility Tools for Bluesky https://www.clrsky.ai/about?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
One-on-One/Small Group x During (Mediating): Sway (matches students with opposing views, facilitated by AI guide). ([swaybeta.ai https://www.swaybeta.ai/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Belief Verification x Dialogue (Gentle Intervention): DebunkBot (Individual disproof through dialogue. Average conspiracy theory belief reduction of about 20% reported in Science). ([Science.org https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adq1814?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Large-scale x After (visualization of consensus and support for deliberation): SocietySpeaks (extracting areas of consensus using Pol.is) / Talk to the City (voice input → transcription, classification, and reporting, sending "voices" back to decision-making). ([societyspeaks.io https://societyspeaks.io/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
What's new?

The design unit is based on paraphrasing, summarizing, reframing, and bridging mutual understanding, rather than leaning too heavily on content "deletion" or "errata labels. The design hypothesis is shared that light interventions before and after speech can restore order without increasing friction. ([techandsocialcohesion.substack.com https://techandsocialcohesion.substack.com/p/heres-how-ai-makes-online-conversations?utm_ source=chatgpt.com])
Evidence.

Not all have been proven, but some studies have emerged that show effect sizes and persistence, such as DebunkBot (effectiveness maintained with tracking). On the other hand, participation induction, scale, and domain generalization remain open questions. ([Science.org https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adq1814?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Implementation Principles (Suggested Governance Perspectives)

Emphasizes choice (opt-in) / transparency / evaluation design (metrics that can be measured on site) / privacy considerations. Creating metrics to measure the quality of dialogue and participation is also recommended. ([toda.org https://toda.org/assets/files/research/blueprint-on-prosocial-tech-design-governance.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Usage to the reader
1. apply your product to the **3 axes (timing x scale x intent)** and discover the blank areas
2. start with an experiment to thinly connect the front-end process (self-reflection nudge) and the back-end process (consensus visualization)
3. measure effectiveness where possible (e.g., re-participation rate, paraphrase adoption rate, stability of consensus areas)

*Supplement: Since the original PDF could not be previewed directly from here due to limitations of the distribution site, we summarized the main points based on the official articles and announcements of the organizers and primary information and peer-reviewed papers of each tool. If necessary, we will reorganize them with PDF page numbers on hand (chapters: Purpose of the survey -> Classification table -> List of tools -> Design guidelines -> Future issues). ([Prosocial Design Network https://www.prosocialdesign.org/blog/report-mapping-llm-tools-for-public-discourse-pluralism-social-cohesion])

[Cartographer] is interesting, but I haven't had a chance to use it.
Why.
That's because I don't like "a situation where many people have to reach a consensus" in the first place, and I live my life by avoiding the composition of the situation.
I do what I want to do and I don't do what I don't want to do, and I cherish this freedom.
My subjectivity determines the allocation of the resources I control, so there is no need for "[collective decision-making].
Well, even with all that said, sometimes I need to do it and I don't like it.
This is probably related to this exchange when Cartographer was used in a regular AI hearing.
>There is an assumption that our resources are exchangeable goods (tokoroten).
>I forgot to share with AI the premise that we are a volunteer organization (nishio).
If our resources are exchangeable goods, and if we are in a situation where collective decision-making determines "what to do with the resources", then Cartographer makes sense,
In reality we are volunteers and "do what we want to do" so there is no need for "collective decision making"
I want to create a personal Cartographer

I am using the term "verbalization system" to mean a system in which AI asks Yes/No questions about things that have not yet been clearly verbalized, and verbalization is encouraged by answering those questions.

[How do I recall a project whose details have been forgotten over time?
I see what you mean.

I've been writing project logs all over Scrapbox as I go along, but over time I lose track of what name and where I've written them. This is especially true when the project does not have a proper name, or when the scope or purpose pivots as it progresses. The logs are all there as data.
Additional information added by looking at the question
No other members to talk to since it is a private project.
All information is in Scrapbox, so it is "centralized".
🔍 "Three Questions" for better self-understanding

On the other hand, the fact that you answered "I don't know" to several questions also gives us a very interesting clue as to where you are in your thinking. In order to further expand your own possibilities, it might be interesting to pause for a moment and consider the following points.
Question #1: Are "discarded ideas" garbage or treasure?

They responded "don't know" about the value of "rejected alternatives" and "causes of failure." These are information that does not appear in the "authentic history" of the decision. However, there may be hidden in them important values and constraints behind the decision-making process, such as "Why didn't you choose that path? Uncovering these factors will further deepen NISHIO's quest for "Why? may further deepen NISHIO's quest for "Why?
Question #2: Is "zero-based thinking" a denial of the past or a new perspective?

We saw hesitation in the options "it is faster to think from scratch" and "it is a good opportunity to think from a zero base." This may be due to the fact that "learning from the past" and "thinking completely new" are seen as opposites in Mr. Nisio's mind. If we were to dare to incorporate a zero-based perspective on the basis of learning from the past, what kind of thinking would emerge?
Question 3: Do you believe in "connections" rather than "rules" of information management?

I was very impressed by his strong "Strong No" response to the suggestion that he should review the rules for information management. This may be an indication of Mr. Nisio's trust in the discoverability of tools such as Scrapbox, rather than the strictness of rules. Perhaps they find value in the organic "connection" between information itself, rather than in rules. This unique sensibility is a powerful weapon unique to Mr. Nisio. How can we make it easier for our future selves to discover these "connections"?
The disorderly logs are not the problem, but the inability to identify the reason for the interruption, 'why is this project stopped in the middle of the project,' is the fundamental problem.
I see
The process of recalling past projects should not be viewed as archaeology to dig up facts, but as an editorial process to rediscover 'new meanings' from a current perspective.
I see
It is more efficient to formulate a "tentative next action" first and then read the logs for the purpose of verifying it, instead of thinking about the next action after recalling the past.
I see

It is precisely when you don't know where you wrote something that it is easier to stop searching intentionally and let chance encounters with Scrapbox's "Random Jump" feature lead to breakthroughs in your thinking.
I don't know if it's a yes or no, but it's interesting.
Suggestion: Take the next step
To help you remember forgotten projects and take the next step, we propose two steps tailored to NISHIO's characteristics.

Step 1] First, proceed on your best route. First, take full advantage of NISHIO's strength, the "Objective Oriented Engine. Formulate a "tentative next action (e.g., "If I were to restart this project, I would first make a prototype of 00"), and then search intensively in Scrapbox with keyword searches and links with the clear objective of verifying it or "identifying the reason for the interruption. This method should be the most satisfactory way to move forward at this point.
Step 2] Try "unexplored routes" as a small experiment. If you get stuck in Step 1 or want a new perspective, why not incorporate just a little "play"? For example,
Decide, "For five minutes a day, I'm going to take a random jump and observe where my thoughts take me."
What if I were to start this project from scratch right now?" and write it out on a new page in Scrapbox.

When air is entrained, it approaches the combustible zone, but is diluted by room temperature air and the temperature drops several hundred degrees Celsius, breaking the auto-ignition temperature (e.g. CO ≈ 609 °C, CH₄ ≈ 537 °C, H₂ ≈ 500-585 °C) and igniting.
I see.[nishio.icon]
What is a diffusion flame?[nishio.icon]
[GPT5.icon]

A diffusion flame (non-premixed flame) is a fire in which the fuel and oxygen (air) are initially unmixed and burn "in place" as they diffuse across the interface. Typical examples include candles, burners with closed air holes, flames over wood or charcoal, and oil pool fires.

Diffusion flame: slow mixing and mixing (diffusion and vortex mixing) rate-determines the rate of combustion. A thin reaction layer (flame sheet) is formed on the equivalent (stoichiometric) surface of the interface.
Fuel rich core (near the gas source) - O₂ is scarce
Reaction layer (flame sheet) - Main reaction proceeds in a thin film where the mixing ratio is equivalent
Outer oxidation zone - secondary oxidation of CO/H₂/soot, etc.

The local temperature of the reaction layer approaches the theoretical flame temperature ~ 1700-2100 °C (depending on the fuel) near the equivalent volume, but actually decreases with radiation and dilution.

At wood and charcoal sites, when the gas rises to ≳800-1000 °C in the equivalent plane and sufficient oxygen is entrained, the diffusion flame is stable and smoke is reduced. Insufficient mixing or cooling in the 600-800 °C range can lead to white/yellow smoke as tar oxidation cannot keep up.
I see, at 600 ℃ on the low side of the charcoal fire, it decomposes and produces gas, but it does not become a flame, it should be 800~1000 ℃ or so.[nishio.icon]
trick[GPT5.icon]
Added when the charcoal bed is more than cherry red (≈700-800°C).
Small amount at a time (10-20% of the current amount by volume) -> preheat at the periphery -> two-stage feeding to the center.
Best timing: The branch you place on the ground ignites in 1-2 seconds.
This looks important, let's put one in, see if it ignites, and pull it out if it looks bad.[nishio.icon]
If you put in a lot without checking, the temperature will drop.
Sear and dry" for 30-90 seconds at the perimeters of the flame, then stand it up and place it over the flame tip after the steam has stopped.
Place 1-2 branches at a time in a grid pattern to create gaps. Thick branches are split to create specific surface area↑.
Temperature range when wood is placed on a charcoal fire
~100 ℃: Drying (removal of free water)
H₂O(l) → H₂O(g) (latent heat of evaporation 2.26 MJ/kg)
150-200 °C: Deacidification, etc. (initial decomposition of hemicellulose, generation of acetic acid and methanol)
200-260 °C: hemicellulose pyrolysis (CO₂, acetic acid, light gas)
240-350 °C: cellulose pyrolysis (levoglucosan = tar main component, CO, CO₂, H₂, CH₄)
280-500 °C: Pyrolysis of lignin (phenols and aromatic tars)
300-400 °C: auto-ignition temperature range of wood surface (condition-dependent)
400-600 °C: Char (charcoal) oxidation predominates, red heat begins
≥600-800 °C: secondary combustion of volatiles and CO/H₂ proceeds and flame stabilizes (tar decomposition also proceeds)
≥700-900+ ℃: Smoke decreases as tar pyrolysis and soot oxidation progresses
Visual guide: dark red 550-650 °C, cherry red 730-800 °C, orange 930-1000 °C
Typical chemical reaction (25 °C standard, standard reaction heat)
Drying and pyrolysis (heat-absorbing and smoke-generating sources)
Drying: H₂O(l) → H₂O(g) +40.7 kJ/mol (= 2.26 MJ/kg)
Wood pyrolysis (schematic): (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ → C_(s) + tar + CO + CO₂ + H₂ + CH₄ + ... (heat absorption, products are condition dependent)
Charcoal/charcoal reaction at surface (solid)
Complete oxidation: C + O₂ → CO₂ -393.5 kJ/mol
Incomplete oxidation: C + ½O₂ → CO -110.5 kJ/mol (increases due to lack of oxygen)
Boudoir reaction: C + CO₂ → 2 CO +172 kJ/mol (strong endothermic → floor temperature decrease)
Aqueous gas reaction: C + H₂O(g) → CO + H₂ +131 kJ/mol (endothermic → floor temperature decrease)
Secondary combustion in gas phase (flame side)
Oxidation of CO: CO + ½O₂ → CO₂ -283 kJ/mol (**faster at about ≥600 °C**)
Oxidation of H₂: H₂ + ½O₂ → H₂O(g) -242 kJ/mol
Oxidation of methane: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O(g) -802 kJ/mol
Approximate temperature for self-ignition and combustion (varies with conditions)
Wood surface: approx. 300-400 °C
CO: approx. 609 °C
H₂: Approx. 500-585 °C
CH₄: approx. 537 °C
Tar vapors: Composition-dependent, but generally easy to ignite at ≥300-500 °C, decompose and burn at ≥700-800 °C**.
Why "adding firewood makes it smoke" (numerical sense)
For 1 kg of firewood with 20% water content, heating 0.2 kg of water to 100 °C (≈63 kJ) + evaporation (≈451 kJ) takes away ≈0.51 MJ.
Furthermore, just raising the wood portion (≈0.8 kg) from 25 to 300 °C results in ≈0.33 MJ (assuming specific heat ≈1.5 kJ/kgK).
Total** ≈ 0.8 MJ or more of heat absorption, the charcoal bed temperature is likely to fall from the 600-800 °C range**.
When the temperature drops to **<600-700 °C, CO secondary combustion slows**, volatiles cannot enter the flame, tar condenses and white/blue smoke is noticeable.
In addition, CO₂/water vapor reacts with charcoal (boudoir/water gas, both endothermic) → cools by following.
In short, the temperature drops due to heat absorption (drying, pyrolysis, gasification) + temporary lack of oxygen,
The temperature does not reach "≥600-800 °C required for vapor phase combustion of the generated gas" → unburned tar/soot = smoke is emitted.

lines.text: Progress is a disturbance of the equilibrium
[development] is [disturbance] of [balance]
[GPT5.icon]
[In Schumpeter's terms, it's like this...

In capitalism, innovation breaks the equilibrium and moves forward, and the adjustment process back to the equilibrium appears as a "recession. The equilibrium itself is not a recession, but rather a "return to equilibrium = painful restructuring". ([schumpeter.info https://schumpeter.info/text2~1.htm?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[static equilibrium = stagnation].

While emphasizing [general equilibrium] of the [Walras] type as [static] ([circulating flow]), we see that neither profit nor interest disappear there and development does not occur = [stagnation]. ([Wikipedia https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%A8%E3%83%BC%E3%82%BC%E3%83%95%E3%83%BB%E3%82%B7%E3%83%A5%E3%83%B3%E3%83%9A%E3%83%BC% E3%82%BF%E3%83%BC?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[Development = disturbance of equilibrium.]

A [new combination] ([innovation]) [breaks the existing equilibrium] and moves the economy forward. It is even stated that "[development and equilibrium are] mutually exclusive. ([Levy Economics Institute of Bard College https://www.levyinstitute.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/wp_1098.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[Recession = Adjustment phase to new equilibrium.]

The period [recession] is when "old factories, methods, and companies" leave the market and a new equilibrium is established through [selection] and [reallocation of resources] after the boom. ([schumpeter.info https://schumpeter.info/text2~1.htm?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

In a nutshell: Equilibrium is not optimal. Equilibrium is stagnation, and the movement back to equilibrium appears as a recession. Progress always comes from imbalance. ([Wikipedia https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%A8%E3%83%BC%E3%82%BC%E3%83%95%E3%83%BB%E3%82%B7%E3%83%A5%E3%83%B3%E3%83%9A%E3%83%BC% E3%82%BF%E3%83%BC?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Note: The Japanese phrase "equilibrium is a depression" is not a literal translation of the cliché, but rather a summary of the above intent (the original is "[Progress is a disturbance of the equilibrium], [a recession is a period of establishing a new equilibrium]," etc.). ([schumpeter.info https://schumpeter.info/text2~1.htm?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
