pages.title: How Talk to the City was created

lines.text: How Talk to the City was created
[GPT5.icon]

It was difficult to achieve both quality and quantity. Existing opinion polls can capture "quantity" but lack "depth" (nuance of open-ended statements), while small-group dialogues can capture "depth" but are weak in "scale. The LLM was created to resolve this trade-off. The official page also clearly states that the aim is to "solve the trade-off between depth and scale. ([Talk to the City https://talktothe.city/about])
Solving the scale x depth tradeoff
Quote: "...solves the trade-off between depth and scale."(T3C's About) ([Talk to the City https://talktothe.city/ about])
Sidenote: The core design concept of LLM solves the classic dilemma of balancing the deep dialogue of a small group of people with the scale of a large survey. In addition, on the top page
Quote: "Focus groups capture nuance, and polls capture scale. T3C does both."

A problematic desire to reverse the spiral of distrust of democracy. The AOI (AI Objectives Institute) cites the motivation to bridge the gap between decision makers and the population by enabling **large-scale, high-speed, inclusive "broad listening "**. The project began with the recognition that there is a lack of means to handle qualitative data on a large scale. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/talk-to-the-city])
Response to the "downward spiral of trust" in democracy
Quote: "...help us escape the spiral of declining trust by allowing us to consult the public in much larger numbers." (Background explanation on the AOI website)
Addendum: The motivation is clearly stated as the issue of restoring trust by allowing voices to be heard in a more mass, faster, and more inclusive way through technological advances.

Direct impetus (initial prototype). The starting point was an early version used for mapping the discourse around AI safety and ethics in early 2023, which was open-sourced in October of the same year. Since then, it has been deployed by AI Assemblies in Taiwan, vTaiwan-based initiatives, etc. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/blog/talk-to-the-city-an-open-source-ai-tool-to- scale-deliberation])
Initial direct aim (to hear the voices of "millions" at the city level)

Quote: "...designed to use a ChatGPT-like interface to survey millions of people in a city."(Wired's article introducing AOI) ([[ WIRED https://www.wired.com/story/peter-eckersley-ai-objectives-institute])
Sidenote: From the early days of AOI's launch, it was envisioned as a pilot for large-scale listening on a city scale.
Product Objective (Accelerate mutual understanding of large numbers of people)
Quote: "Talk to the City helps large groups of people coordinate by understanding each other better, faster, and in more depth."
Tip: The goal is not to simply generate a summary, but to reduce it to a form that can be used for consensus building and decision making while retaining nuance.
Research-based rationale (quality x quantity)
Quote: "Existing processes... must trade off scale for qualitative detail... In contrast, frontier LLMs enable rich qualitative data at scale." (Policy Recommendations Report)
Supplement: The need to overcome the limitations of conventional methods (scale or depth) with LLM is shown as background.
In short, the challenge is to **"take a large number of voices, including free-form ones, and turn them into a decision-useful form quickly, while preserving their nuance.

In short, the scale and depth of Talk to the City was directly inspired by the challenge to "quickly "spread the word" on a city to national scale while preserving the nuances of free speech". ([ai.objectives.institute https://ai.objectives.institute/talk-to-the-city-landing])
Sources are these two.
“Talk to the City helps large groups of people coordinate by understanding each other better, faster, and in more depth.”
→ Top headline on the official Talk to the City home page. ([Talk to the City https://talktothe.city/])
“Existing processes… must trade off scale for qualitative detail… In contrast, frontier LLMs enable rich qualitative data at scale.”
→ AI4Democracy report, "How can AI be used to inform policymaking?" (Turan & McKenzie, 2024) Introduction, p. 4.
Just a quick point 👇.
Formal utilization and collaboration at the government level

AOI stated that "AOI worked with Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Development (moda) and used T3C to analyze large opinion data at AI Assemblies and other events in 2023. moda operates its own T3C instance." ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/talk-to-the-city-landing])
The first place of introduction is "Alignment Assemblies".

In October 2023, the head of T3C discussed with Minister Audrey Tang and others in Taipei. He explained that the first deployment was the "Alignment Assemblies" organized by moda, and that T3C visualized and organized the opinions collected online in Polis. Details are also available on the official moda page. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/blog/amplifying-voices-talk-to-the-city-in-taiwan ])
Complementary relationship with vTaiwan/Polis

vTaiwan collects opinions in Polis → T3C clusters and summarizes free-texts, and incorporates them into Taiwan's deliberation process. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/blog/amplifying-voices-talk-to-the-city-in-taiwan ])
Public Mention (Audrey Tang)

In December 2023, Tang Feng introduced T3C as a concrete example in a webinar at LSE IDEAS, stating that T3C is a technology that combines diversity and scale. ([govinsider.asia https://govinsider.asia/intl-en/article/turning-conflicts-into-co-creation-taiwans-digital-ministry-moda- harnesses-digital-policy-for-democracy])
In addition, T3C official Tang Feng's comments were also published ("The cost is virtually zero... "broad-listing"). ([Talk to the City https://talktothe.city/])
Specific Use Cases in Taiwan

AI Assembly 2023: Collected more than 2,000 opinions from more than 400 people and provided topic grouping and interactive viewing at T3C. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/blog/amplifying-voices-talk-to-the-city-in-taiwan ])

Same-sex marriage (on the agenda of the government's JOIN platform): the case is presented based on T3C's analysis of JOIN's mass comments. The original data is from the Legal Department's discussion page. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/blog/amplifying-voices-talk-to-the-city-in-taiwan ])

∙ Post-2024 presidential election analysis by party (KMT/DPP): report on Media Readr data by T3C. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/blog/amplifying-voices-talk-to-the-city-in-taiwan ])
designation
Sometimes introduced in communications for Taiwan as **Chinese name "我城對談 "**. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/blog/amplifying-voices-talk-to-the-city-in-taiwan ])

In summary, T3C is used by both government and civil society as a "broadband" infrastructure to complement vTaiwan/Polis, in conjunction with Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs (moda). The "vTaiwan/Polis" is used by both the government and civil society. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/talk-to-the-city-landing])

[GPT5.icon]

The most important "impetus" was the desire to visualize and extract consensus through technology when faced with the problem of "voices gathering but not seeing consensus/constructive convergence" in large-scale, decentralized movements such as Occupy and the Arab Spring. The company was founded by Colin Megill et al. (Christopher Small and Michael Bjorkegren), which later resulted in a design that "visualizes clusters without a reply button + voting". ([GeekWire https://www.geekwire.com/2014/startup-spotlight-polis/])

As a supplementary note, it is said that the use of vTaiwan after Sunflower in Taiwan was the turning point, and that Audrey Tang and CL Kao were instrumental in the push to open source the software. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pol.is])
[Sunflower Student Movement]

“No reply button – hence no trolling.” ([WIRED https://www.wired.com/story/taiwan-democracy-social-media/])
Background inspiration (e.g., Arab Spring)

(Summary) From Megill's own explanation and interviews at the time, the "difficulty of bringing together many voices constructively "** that was exposed in a large and decentralized movement directly led to the creation of Polis as a design that could converge even with a large number of people (no reply button, etc.**), and at the 2016 g0v summit We can confirm that it has been open-sourced.

pages.title: Nature and use of tools for conviviality

lines.text: Nature and use of tools for conviviality
About [Nodal Point of Thought 2022-01-05
[GPT5.icon]
Design and evaluate tools on two levels: "tool characteristics" and "usage (operation).

Conviviality, as Iriichi put it, was to liberate people from the status of "mere consumers" and give them the freedom to [create and remake] in order to [take care of] themselves and their surroundings.
Hence, X must satisfy,
(1) Plasticity (giving itself shape),
(2) Orientation toward mutual aid (toward generating help for someone else),
(3) Limitations as a device (avoid abuse and concentration)
The three points are

On the other hand, Zoom and other tools are sufficiently convivial and "usable "** as tools, but depending on how they are used, they can also become "mere consumers of meetings. It is necessary to face the two layers of tool x practice.
2) Implications for each X (two layers of tools x usage)
groupware
Nature of the tool: Users can create and modify their own information systems for use in their work (e.g., kintone).
Usage: Can you "design a care package" to help others do their work? Yes has already been demonstrated here.
Metaverse / Virtual Office
Nature of the tool: "our place" can be edited and extended (like a Minecraft server).
Usage: Not only do we enter a given world, but we rework the place to suit our purposes.
SNS
Properties of the tool: forkability, algorithmic transparency, data portability.
Usage: Do not be carried away by the audience mode (passive scrolling), but set up circuits of generation, editing and co-production.
Video conferencing (Zoom)
Nature of the instrument: There can be freedom to choose one's own partner and content.
Usage: **Close to "only participate when called" ** to become non-convivial. Design is sufficient, operation is the key.
3) Conjunction with SECI and "living/thinking
Contribution to SECI
It is a good tool to turn the flow of "expression of moyamoya (tacit knowledge) → connection of fragments → internalization through practice" into a low-friction process.
It is suggestive to organize that Keichobot can help with expressivization and Kozaneba can help with articulation, which can also contribute to internalization of difficult text comprehension.
It is better to allow the tools to overlap in any order, rather than assuming the doctrine that co-creation and manifestation occur "alternately".
Dwell-think
Along the lines of Heidegger/Gendlin, understanding is "living in the form" of the object.
X should provide a **"place to live "**, and the key is UI/expressiveness that can "work" (return to the essence) the viewpoints, relationships, and meanings of words.
4) Evaluation criteria (checklist)
A. Nature of tools (product design)
1. plasticity: schema editing, scripting, and UI composing
2. forkability/portability: easy to fork and export data, spaces, and apps
3. locality and marginalization: small autonomy over mass distribution and centralized control
4. transparency: key algorithms and authority models can be understood and adjusted
5. cross-border hubness: there are pathways to bring in external knowledge without permissions (external linkage, import, guest permissions)
B. Usage (operation and culture)
6) Habit of expressing mumbling: first in short sentences, including "emotional words" (e.g., Keichobot)
7) Rituals of consolidation: devote time to the connection and rearrangement of the fragments (Kozaneba, etc.)
8) Design for care: produce the smallest unit of generation that reliably makes the work of others easier.
9) External inflow: Permanent circuits to bring in knowledge from complementary vendors and external communities (a measure to mitigate path dependency)
10) Reduce "spectator mode": always have a conduit to connect meetings and timelines to production and editing (also use Zoom convivially).
5) Anti-patterns ("non-convivial" smells)
Vendor lock-in assumption/export difficulties
Eclecticism that invites passive consumption in rankings and notifications
Only "finished templates" and not editable in structure or behavior
High "persuasion costs" due to the dependence on approval as a source of external information (contributing to the prisoner's dilemma of acquiring knowledge from outside the company).
6) Methods of measurement (hypotheses and indicators)
Hypothesis H1: As conviviality is increased, SECI's expressivization, concatenation, and internalization turn faster and deeper.
Hypothesis H2: Increasing "[permissionless cross-border]" will decrease path dependency bias and increase knowledge diversity.
Observation index (example)
Generation ratio: Ratio of new generation/alteration to consumptive browsing
Reuse/forking rate: Number of reallocations and derivations of others' results
Number of cross-border introductions: number of concepts and tools brought in from outside communities
Persuasion cost proxy indicators: rate of small book purchases and trial experiments that do not require prior approval, etc.
7) Small experimental design (2 weeks)
Every morning for 10 minutes: Each individual expresses his/her "moyamoya" in 3 lines (Keichobot). Someone connects one or more "moyamoya" on the same day (Kozaneba).
2. 2 times a week for 30 minutes: "Placemaking Session" - Modification of one existing workspace or world to add a "caretaking tool" (form, bot, in-world object, etc.)
3. at the end of every week: invite one person from outside/another organization to show/touch the permission-less.
4. manually measure the above indicators with a minimum of logs and inspect for anti-patterns.
summary

X can be a **"tool for conviviality "** if we have the two layers of the nature of the tool (plasticity, mutual aid orientation, marginalization) and the way it is used (the practice of expressing, connecting, and internalizing, the circuit of transcending borders). The duality of the Minecraft server, the kintone case study, and Zoom already illustrate the importance of both layers.

Furthermore, I believe that designing and operating tools as a "place to live" by overlapping the perspectives of "build, live, and think" will boost the precision of understanding (dwell-think) and the creation of knowledge (SECI).
If necessary, this evaluation criteria can be put into a diagnostic sheet that applies to a specific X (your current SNS/virtual space/groupware).

[https://gyazo.com/46f3b5e4bfc5c3a21a00ebd01f22176e]

[The reason for the creation of the IdoBata system].
[GPT5.icon]

The trigger was DD2030's "Large-Scale Deliberative Discussion Platform Concept" that began in January 2025. From this concept, the product name was materialized as "Idobata System". ([type https://type.jp/et/feature/29497/])

The purpose is to turn large scale deliberations with AI for Japan (to overcome majority vote bias and voice dissipation) while learning from Taiwan's JOIN and vTaiwan The official DD2030 "Idobata" introduction clearly states its design intent. ([Digital Democracy 2030 https://dd2030.org/idobata])

The origin of the name shares the history of how it was established through association and abstraction from the Japanese words "Idobata-Kaigi" and "Tokyo AI Strategy Idobata-Kaigi". ([/villagepump/idobata-system])
Repository release move was announced in mid-March 2025 (record of Plurality Tokyo Namerakaigi timing). ([Large-scale deliberation support system "Idobata"] )

In short, IIDOBATA was launched to implement DD2030's "Japan's version of large-scale deliberation in the AI age," and was created as a foundation for "collecting, organizing, and translating into policy" in a single step, based on successful examples from Taiwan. --This is the starting point of IIDOBATA. ([Digital Democracy 2030 https://dd2030.org/idobata])

IIDOBATA system v2
[The reason for the creation of the "IdoBata System v2".]
There is the Idobata system v1, which uses Discourse, and the Idobata system v2, which now interacts with AI. What is the reason for this switch?
[Regular Meeting Minutes https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cK5i3ATo1OXsy-oicllY6-YlI-q0AJVtqQW7a71V-AU/edit?tab=t.fax1253vkyvp]
[GPT5.icon]
Weak participation leads (bulletin board type friction)
The procedure to "come, read, and write" to Discourse was so heavy that we could not move enough people even in the X collaboration experiment on 3/26. People leave before gathering on the Discourse.
Operational cost of manpower facilitation assumptions

In the bulletin board type, summarizing, organizing arguments, and responding to flaming tends to be manpower intensive, and the burden of ongoing operation is high. Even in the experiment, "pre/post-processing to circulate the discussion" was heavy.
Redefine experience value (immediate reflection to the core)

Decided to focus on "interacting with AI → my comments are immediately reflected in the report" as the greatest Wow experience at the 4/9 policy consolidation, and stated that Discourse integration will be lowered as a priority.
Delivery time and safety requests

In order to be ready for actual operation between May and July, we need a structure that can be quickly turned around in a "single flow". An AI interactive UI that can be completed by itself is safer and faster than external BBS integration.
Avoiding Technical Complexity
We disliked the complexity of integration, authentication, hosting, and moderation, and opted for a single product design to complete the process.

In short, v1 (Discourse-linked bulletin board type) had high participation friction and operational burden, and was weak in "immediate visualization" of value. Therefore, for v2, we switched to an interactive type where the AI takes the role of listener and organizer, and the structured results are returned on the spot - that was the reason at the time.

pages.title: The reason for the creation of the broadband AI

lines.text: The reason for the creation of the broadband AI
[GPT5.icon]

After the continuous deployment of AOI's Talk to the City in Japan, the need for non-engineering and "in-depth analysis" became apparent, and "Broadband AI" was derived and redesigned in response to this need. ([Digital Democracy 2030 https://dd2030.org/kouchou-ai])
Starting Point (2023): AI Objectives Institute deploys Talk to the City (TTTC) as open source. The origins of broadband AI can be found here.

Actual application in Japan (2024): TTTC was used in the Tokyo gubernatorial election to visualize statements made on X, and was also used in the subsequent coverage of the lower house election. Practical issues were identified.

Learning from long-term strategic projects (2024/11-2025/1): The "[Shin Tokyo 2050]" project by Tokyo Metropolitan Government x GovTech Tokyo clarified the needs for hierarchical digging and extraction of dense clusters. The necessary functions of the public hearing AI were organized. ([NOTE (NOTE) https://note.com/nishiohirokazu/n/nb37adf96fe50])

Embodiment (functional requirements): Modification of TTTC to suit the practices of Japanese local governments and politicians, such as CSV uploading for operations that non-engineers can also turn around, and extraction of dense clusters.
Open to the public (3/16/2025): Open-source release of a public hearing AI as Digital Democracy 2030. Subsequent to community development. ([Digital Democracy 2030 https://dd2030.org/kouchou-ai])

In a nutshell, we needed to bridge the gap between "TTTC's ability to collect a large number of voices "quickly and widely" and "the operational and analytical requirements for "deep and sure" use in the field. The need to bridge this gap was the impetus for the project.

Cartographer says
Mr. Nishio strongly believes that the attraction of [DD2030] is "being involved in the chaotic creative scene where new products are born.
>Yes: As a first point of contact, it is more appealing to show an ongoing "live discussion" than to show a highly finished product or philosophy.
>Yes: The website should honestly disclose the real struggles of the organization, not just the clean philosophy.
>Strong Yes: A culture that welcomes and shares "quality failures," where the knowledge that "this approach didn't work" accumulates, is essential.

Thought experiment: if you post the opinion "cats are cute" in any discussion, for example, it will appear as a point of agreement with high agreement from both camps.

pages.title: How Talk to the City's Turbo showed up

lines.text: How Talk to the City's Turbo showed up
[Talk to the City Turbo]
[GPT5.icon]
I'll try to get to the point of why Turbo appeared later, using "primary information in English" to back it up.

Separation of roles is clearly stated in the README: The repository README defines Turbo as "graph-based... generates interactive reports, and a very wide variety of LLM apps," while Reports ( Scatter) is positioned as "CLI-based... static interactive scatter-plot reports. = It can be read that Turbo was introduced as a vessel for a group of LLM apps and interactivity. ([GitHub https://github.com/AIObjectives/talk-to-the-city-reports])
Accelerate "LLM-based feature development" in spring 2024 (i.e., expansion pressure from static Scatter)
Improved chat merge (2024-03-07) introduced conversational exploration. ([GitHub https://github.com/AIObjectives/talk-to-the-city-reports/commits/main/])

Chat should work with multi-lingual (translated) reports Issue (2024-03-28) = Request to use chat even with translated reports. ([GitHub https://github.com/AIObjectives/talk-to-the-city-reports/issues/179])

A series of operational and distribution-oriented features were introduced, including Add Ability to Translate Reports (2024-03-27) and Add switch to set report to Private/Public (2024-04-17). ([GitHub https://github.com/AIObjectives/talk-to-the-city-reports/commits/main/])

These are natural as a context that required a separate system (=Turbo) that encompasses "LLM functionality + operational requirements" (also consistent with the separation of roles in the README). ([GitHub https://github.com/AIObjectives/talk-to-the-city-reports])

Limitations on the Scatter side are also apparent in the Issue: Scatter Reports specific UI issues such as zoom limits and tooltip updates in dense clusters are reported, suggesting field needs that are difficult to explore in depth with only a static scatterplot-centric experience (2025-02-16). ([GitHub https://github.com/AIObjectives/talk-to-the-city-reports/issues/197])

Product Direction (original explanation): The AOI/Official is to "solve the "depth/scale trade-off" with LLMs" and "interactively explore and summarize large-scale qualitative data," and Turbo's design (graph infrastructure + various The design of Turbo (graph infrastructure + various LLM apps) is an embodiment of this policy. ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/talk-to-the-city-landing?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Explicit trigger for transition: commit "T3C-413: Update README to point to new repo" on 2025-07-31 officially marks the shift in the development center of gravity (archiving the old mono repo and directing it to the new implementation system). ([GitHub https://github.com/AIObjectives/talk-to-the-city-reports/commits/main/])
Summary (Conclusion)

Looking at the primary English information base, the demand for "dynamic and multi-functional analysis workflows" such as LLM chat/translation/publication/private management, etc., rose dramatically in the spring of 2024, and since static scatter plot reports (Scatter) alone could not cover the demand, the Turbo system with its graph infrastructure ＋The separation of roles description in the README, the sequence of issues/commits at the time, and the official design philosophy are all evidence of this. ([GitHub https://github.com/AIObjectives/talk-to-the-city-reports])

pages.title: The age of oligopoly of knowledge of transcendent beings

lines.text: The age of oligopoly of knowledge of transcendent beings
An era of [knowledge oligopoly] of [transcendent beings
[Knowledge oligopoly]
[knowledge]  /  [oligopoly]
[GPT5.icon]
That's a nice phrase, "an age of oligopoly in the knowledge of transcendent beings."
A rough breakdown reveals the following composition:
1. what does "transcendent being" mean?
It used to be plainly "[god]" or "religious [transcendent]," but now I think it can be taken a little broader.
That which cannot be physically and cognitively grasped by a single person
Huge AI model
Financial Markets & Global Economy
National surveillance system
Climate systems and huge infrastructures
A black box that in itself cannot fully explain "what it is doing" or "why it is doing it" even to the parties involved
These things act as "beings beyond our side" from our everyday sense.
2. once "[theology]" and now "[AI studies]"
Just as biblical knowledge was oligopolized by Latin and the clergy in medieval Europe,
Model Blueprint
learning data
Statistical properties and limitations of the output
The design concept of the social system that incorporates it
and other "meta-knowledge about transcendent systems" is concentrated in a very small number of companies, states, and experts.
I envision a "[new] priestly class" that monopolizes [interpretation] and [justification], without the public being able to directly verify "why the decision was made the way it was.
[priestly rank].
[priest].
3. what is at stake?
As this composition proceeds:
The source of the norm is obscured.
Norms are pushed out in the form of "because the AI said so" or "because this is the result of the model," while the reason for the decision remains invisible.
The objection interface is lost.
Even if you feel, "That doesn't seem right," you can't break it down to see where to question it.
The government and companies tend to be in a state of "I don't know, but it's probably right".
[democracy] becomes "[oracle consulting]"
Rather than "citizens + representatives" deliberating and deciding,
The "citizen input → transcendent system → the few who control its interpretation" takes the real power of decision-making.
4. it seems better to treat "oligopoly of knowledge" and "transcendence" separately
To summarize, there are at least two axes:
1. degree of transcendence
All human beings can understand everything ↔ Structurally unintelligible
2. knowledge distribution
Open and anyone can learn ↔ Information and know-how are monopolized by a few
The danger is in the "highly transcendent and oligopolistic knowledge" quadrant.
On the contrary,
Even if the system is transcendental.
Open model, data, and design philosophy
Plural, contestable (multiple lineages exist)
Education and visualization is in place for the general public to learn.
Then there will be room to tame "transcendence" successfully.
5. questions that could be considered from here on

Formal utilization and collaboration at the government level

AOI stated that "AOI worked with Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Development (moda) and used T3C to analyze large opinion data at AI Assemblies and other events in 2023. moda operates its own T3C instance." ([AI - Objectives - Institute https://ai.objectives.institute/talk-to-the-city-landing])

Complementary relationship with vTaiwan/Polis

Public Mention (Audrey Tang)

lines.text: Determining KPIs is not a human task.
Once you determine [the KPI], it ceases to be [the work of the man].
When KPIs are determined, it is more efficient for an AI to do the work than for a human to do it according to those KPIs.
Because AI outperforms humans in the speed of "improvement activities" on the scale defined by KPIs.
So (while there is room for human work in the short term), in the long term, once the KPI is set, it is no longer human work.
From the point of view of those who have come to the idea that, once the KPI is determined, it appears to be "a job that will not be a human job in the future" and "a job with no future".
If it is possible to run away, run away.

Software 2.0
[GPT5.icon]
To put it bluntly:
Software 2.0 = "automation of tasks for which procedures cannot be written but can be checked for correctness"
This is the story.
1.Software 1.0 ↔ 2.0 Contrast
The original framework of [Karpathy] was:
Software 1.0
A world where humans write all procedures (algorithms) such as if / for in code
The "if you can explain the rules, you can automate them" worldview
Software 2.0
The learned model itself, such as a neural net, is the program.

A worldview in which humans decide only the "objective function (evaluation metric)," "data," and "network structure," and the rest is an automatic search for programs with good learning (gradient descent or RL) ([Wikipedia https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_2.0?utm_ source=chatgpt.com])
Here's what Karpathy had to say recently
Software 1.0 automated what we could explain.
Software 2.0 automates what we can verify. ([Medium https://medium.com/illumination/software-2-0-and-the-strange-shape-of-ai-progress-072e00c7dd94])
and recapitulating.
What is "automation of verifiable things"?
Here verifiable is a task that satisfies approximately the following conditions
1. results can be scored mechanically
Can be evaluated numerically with correct and incorrect answers, scores, loss functions, etc.
2. reset the environment and try again and again
High speed trial and error in simulator/test environment, etc.

3. automatically given valuations (reward / loss is automatic) ([Blockchain News https://blockchain.news/flashnews/ai-software-2-0-and-verifiability-trading- implications-for-crypto-markets-btc-eth-from-karpathy-in-2025])
The argument is that these tasks are clear bait (feedback) for gradient descent and reinforcement learning, so Software 2.0 (AI) can easily improve on its own, i.e., it can be automated.
3. specific examples (strong areas)
Verifiable and good at Software 2.0
coding
If you run the test, it will automatically tell you if it passes or not.
Math problems (theorem proving and calculation problems)
Checking for correct answers is mechanical.
Speech recognition, image recognition, structured data extraction
Match against labeled data and you get a score.
Games (Go, Chess, Atari, etc.)
Clear win/loss/score, and the environment can be reset as much as you want.
These areas are not suitable for LLMs and RLs.

The view is that it is easy to go all the way to beyond the top human at once, because you can turn "try a lot of things and grade them → update parameters" at high speed. ([Medium https://medium.com/illumination/software-2-0-and-the-strange-shape-of-ai-progress-072e00c7dd94])
Conversely, areas that are not so verifiable
Creative writing ("interesting" and "literary value" of novels and essays)
Long-term strategy and policy development
Decisions based on social context (politics, human resources, interpersonal negotiations)
"Is this design cool?" Aesthetic evaluations such as
These are
There is no single correct answer.
Scoring criteria depend on human subjectivity
Feedback is slow or noisy
Therefore, it is difficult to automatically calculate the score and learn.

In Karpathy's terms, this is an area where full automation by Software 2.0 is unlikely to progress due to low verifiability. ([Medium https://medium.com/illumination/software-2-0-and-the-strange-shape-of-ai-progress-072e00c7dd94])
5. summary: what Karpathy has to say
once upon a time
→Can it be written as an algorithm?" is the boundary of automation (Software 1.0)
From now on.
→Can the results be automatically verified?" is the boundary of automation (Software 2.0)
In other words, Software 2.0 = automation of verifiable tasks (tasks for which results can be judged mechanically as good or bad).
In other words, it is a guideline for thinking about what kind of jobs and fields will be swallowed by AI.

lines.text: Smoothing the conflict between lickety-split and conflict
Smoothing the conflict between [velvety] and [confrontation].
Discussion from [dd2030 slack] [DivCon
Shinta Nakayama (tokoroten)
By putting out the "conflict axis," you've lost the "smooth."
Smooth things are no longer smooth.
I'm starting to understand Ken's obsession with scatter plots, and those are "smooth".
Scatter plots as a tool to recognize "smoothness
It's a scatterplot as a tool to capture complexity as it is complex, but if you don't have the ability to demand there, you're not going to get insight, and that's what you're going to get.
NISHIO Hirokazu
Scatter diagram as a complex expression, conflict as a simple expression, then it would be good if we could show the scatter diagram and then simplify it like a slider (miscellaneous idea).
I'm starting to think that "scatter plots are smooth" is an important concept, but it's too big a leap to explain to the general public, so I'd like to crunch it down a bit more into language.

Scatter plots are visualizations of distributions, and when the axes are shown, the "two ends" are shown, and the actual distribution of people's opinions, which should be distributed between the two ends, is discarded.
Proposal 1: Create 5 "strongly agree to strongly disagree" divisions on the axis

Proposal 2: Include an intermediate group in addition to the "strongly agree" and "strongly disagree" groups, but from that group, discard passive opinions like "I'm not sure" and actively extract opinions that are not favorable to being in either the "agree or disagree" group and put them in the opinion examples.

To put it very abstractly, the conflict is two dots, and you create "[half-way-done] dots," and the choice of which of the many options you choose should be interesting, not stale. If you filter out the existing ones, the repeated "[delving into]" will create more and more details, approaching a continuous, smooth description. By approaching the representation of "complex things as complex" only in the minimum necessary areas based on the reader's interest, cognitive capacity is less likely to overflow.
[GPT5.icon]
The conflict is first expressed as two points.
Make a "point of middle division" against it.
At this point, there are many possible candidates for the middle division, but the one that is interesting, not clichéd, should be selected from among them.
Once the middle split is chosen, the "newly generated point" becomes the edge of the conflict, not the original two points.
A further mid-split can be performed for the two new points.
By repeatedly dividing the middle while filtering out what is already there, the description becomes more and more detailed with each "dig," approaching a continuous and smooth expression.
Based on the reader's interest, by approaching the representation of "complex things as complex" only to the minimum necessary, the cognitive capacity is less likely to be flooded.

pages.title: My slow self is the bottleneck, but I'm still moving fast and smart overall.

lines.text: My slow self is the bottleneck, but I'm still moving fast and smart overall.
[GPT5.icon]

In a world where AI moves much faster, we need to abandon the assumption that we control the process by ourselves while understanding it all. Humans will become designers of objectives, constraints, and evaluation axes, rather than process supervisors, leaving the AI to explore, implement, and self-document (log, summarize, version control), with another AI in charge of testing and reviewing as well. Humans would periodically check only the output and decide "what to consider a problem" and "what meaning to give to which proposal. Even if you can't fully grasp the process, you only need to have a grip on the entry, exit, and rewind mechanisms. You cannot change the fact that you are slow, but there is no need to slow down the entire process because of your slowness. You are the bottleneck, but if you use your slowness as a filter, you can move faster and smarter as a whole.
[https://gyazo.com/6068456f18d27c4f25e7263deab8e526]
A: Before AI, humans moved slower, so there was more scope for grasping
B: With the advent of AI, the speed at which human-AI pairs moved increased, but the speed was still within the grasp of humans
The extent of the "graspable range" may vary from person to person
May differ from task to task.
C: And then it accelerates even further, beyond what we can grasp, to the point where people say, "What? What do you mean?" and it's like, "Oh, what?
It's a mistake for humans and AI to keep pace in the first place.
D: AI should use its high speed to search outside the range of human observation
We can then suggest to the human, "After studying Proposals 1, 2, and 3, I think that Proposal 3 is promising, so let's take this course of action.
People can say no to that, of course.
I could say explore more ideas like this.
[** latitude]
[nishio.icon]
[https://gyazo.com/82fb8fc67dfd45134df0b0ba495e1edf]
When AI accelerates [ideas] and they go outside [the range of human grasp], we don't know how to bring them back because we haven't [grasped] them.
Isn't it correct to rate something that moves faster than you at your own speed?
How can I make sure that I, as a slow being, don't become a bottleneck?
[GPT5.icon]

It would be easier to sort out the "problem of slow self-discipline of fast things" and the "problem of not being able to return to it once you can no longer grasp it" if they were handled separately.
1. separate roles: don't make it a goal to "understand it all".
❌ A human being keeps track of every single thing that is happening.
✅ Humans hold "objectives and constraints" and "evaluations" and AI moves at high speed toward them.
2. mandate "human compression" for fast processes
Create a layered structure
L0: Raw trace (read by AI)
L1: Short, step-by-step summary
L2: Human-readable "progress report" in one minute
L3: A human being can read in 10 minutes, "Summary of Background and Implications."
You usually only see L2 or L3.

But if you can "dig to L1/L0 only where you are interested," you can expand only where you need to, assuming you don't follow the whole thing, so it is less likely to break down even if there is a speed difference.
3. "Can't revert" problems can be resolved by version control.
The reason it is difficult to know how to revert is because it is unclear where to start and where to end a "certain single change".
4. let the fast ones audit each other (let AI audit AI)
5. focus human work on "orienting" and "making sense
AI: Mass generation, search, trial and error
Humans:.
What is considered a problem (problem setting)
Which indicators to focus on (design of evaluation axes)
Making sense of the ideas that emerged, making narratives, and connecting them to society

Only a human being can say not only "Which proposal did you adopt?" but also "Why this proposal?" and "What does it mean to you?" Only a human being can do this, so we intentionally reserve this part as a human task.

lines.text: Clarify that municipalities can publish OSS
[https://www.youtube.com/live/HmX5VoFPzIA?si=fug7mPXEUFwObuP4&t=17679]
>[takahiroanno https://x.com/takahiroanno/status/1993208906781495749] It's my first question in parliament.

> We asked about legal barriers to the use of OSS by local governments (issues related to the handling of property under the Local Autonomy Law) and received a clear answer from Minister of Internal Affairs and Communications Yoshimasa Hayashi: "It is possible for local governments to open source software they have developed and make it available to others.
>[ihara2525 https://x.com/ihara2525/status/1993243046969065610] Thank you! We will do our best at GovTech Tokyo to provide more and more case studies next time!
>[takahiroanno https://x.com/takahiroanno/status/1993276009035317444] It has been a while! Thank you for the reply. We are looking forward to your future activities!
>[hal_sk https://x.com/hal_sk/status/1993225968434168273] I am so glad to hear this! Thanks for the great question!
>[takahiroanno https://x.com/takahiroanno/status/1993276186966081951] Thanks for getting back to me! I'm glad we were able to get through the first step, the legal interpretation part~!
>[maki_makirou https://x.com/maki_makirou/status/1993248645794443719] Thank you for suddenly getting to the heart of the matter.
> If possible, we would appreciate it if you could go so far as to issue a notice from the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications.
> I would like to leave it in a more concrete form.
>[takahiroanno https://x.com/takahiroanno/status/1993276534321561766] I have already asked for a further question about the notification. I am happy to proceed with this!
>[maki_makirou https://x.com/maki_makirou/status/1993281108361068725] so great I cried...
Related Explanations

>[nagise https://x.com/nagise/status/1993327209696968899] 《Works such as software and programs owned by local governments do not fall under public property under Article 238 of the Local Autonomy Law, and program copyrights do not fall under administrative property under the same article. Therefore, they can be released as open source software without severe restrictions. Is that the interpretation of the MIC?
>[nagise https://x.com/nagise/status/1993327549682958454] This is a very good cut. It would be interesting to see municipal sources converted to OSS.

> "People are hesitant to open source and utilize software because they are concerned that 'software copyrights may be considered administrative property. It is stipulated that administrative property cannot be leased or rights transferred without permission.
>[nagise https://x.com/nagise/status/1993329390177185826] Well, even if they can legally release the code, whether the field actually wants to release it is another story. ......
>[nagise https://x.com/nagise/status/1993329646092665074] It would be reassuring for those who want to go public to confirm that there is no legal problem, no wall there.

>[hal_sk https://x.com/hal_sk/status/1993225780542029854] Oh, a clear answer from the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications to the long-standing issue of OSS disclosure by local governments! It's OK to open OSS to the public, municipalities!
> The question starts around 4:54. The issue of interpretation of [Article 238 of the Local Autonomy Law], which is mentioned here, has been explained in the past in my NOTE.
[Limitations of creating a system for each municipality｜Hal Seki https://note.com/hal_sk/n/nd992ea322c78]

>[honisher https://x.com/honisher/status/1993538898568659371] Seki, I have a question: you mean that there are municipalities "other than TMG" that manage and operate assets that would be open to OSS. What kind of scale and how many are there? Please let me know as much as you know. As a countryside government official, I have no idea. What kind of local governments are you talking about, and what kind of demographics are you talking about?
>[hal_sk https://x.com/hal_sk/status/1993577605174571301] First of all, I think it is great that TMG will be able to do this.
> It is still fresh in our minds that the Tokyo Metropolitan Government's Corona countermeasure site was released as open source and reused in nearly 80 communities.

> At that time, we were able to provide open source without any problems, but it is worthwhile to be able to release the information without the fear of being tipped off. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government has also created OSS guidelines.

> I can't give specific municipality names for other consultation cases due to confidentiality obligations, but there are many at the government-designated city level that want to do this kind of thing.
> Naturally, I am more suited to apps and web systems, not the kind of work that uses packages.
> In addition, the original data integration platform is open source, and there is a need to release related items as OSS.

> Rather than releasing the entire system as OSS, it is possible to do something meaningful without a large municipality, considering things like libraries for data conversion, QGIS plugins, kintone templates, Gemini Gem source code, etc.
> In fact, there is a case in which [Kakogawa City] provided a template for an online application system for a special fixed benefit as "open data
[Kakogawa City version of online application system for special fixed benefits - Dataset - Kakogawa City Open Data API https://opendata-api-kakogawa.jp/ckan/dataset/tokubetuteigakukyuuhukin]

>[hal_sk https://x.com/hal_sk/status/1993530224047538606] OSS and open data provided by public organizations are sometimes called "digital public goods". There will be a talk by Cheryl from UNICEF, who promotes digital public goods globally, and a board game session to learn about OSS, so if you are interested in this matter, please join us!
[Code for Japan Summit https://summit.code4japan.org/]

>[hal_sk https://x.com/hal_sk/status/1993530224047538606] I'd like to write my thoughts on this matter, since some people say that "most municipalities can't develop systems in-house", "most operations are packaged", "you can't maintain OSS if you use it", and so on. I would like to write my thoughts on this issue.
> I didn't ask what Team Mirai thinks, so this is just my personal opinion.
> I'm not saying that OSS is a silver bullet or that all systems should be OSS.
> We are not even discussing in-house production, because if what some local governments have developed can be open-sourced, other vendors can use it to develop their systems.
> There may indeed be systems that cannot be maintained, but that's fine. If someone needs it, just maintain it. That is OSS.
> In fact, there are people in the municipal field who want to convert to OSS but have not been able to do so, and we are consulting with them.
> "I can now do things I wanted to do but couldn't before."
> That's wonderful enough in my opinion. We are not forced to do it.
> note, I have written about some specifics.

>[hal_sk https://x.com/hal_sk/status/1993559418714357828] It was actually 11 years ago that we received a consultation from a local government asking us if we would like to convert a system we had created to OSS. The vendor was also open to the possibility of expanding its commercial distribution, and was willing to welcome the opportunity if the system they had created could be expanded and lead to solutions to their problems.
> However, that is where Article 238 of the Local Autonomy Law stands in the way. If the software work ordered is the property of the municipality, it may not be possible to rent it free of charge.
> I can't give you a clear answer if the legislator puts it to you.
> I had to give up in the end at that time.

> Then we run into this problem several times a year. Even though the digital department wanted to push for OSS release as a policy, it was difficult to gain understanding. Such a situation has continued.

> Although we clearly raised this issue at last year's Digital Administrative and Financial Reform Conference in a dialogue to identify issues, we were not able to get the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications to issue an open notice after that.

> Even though the national government has been pushing the concept of "digital public goods," there has been a long wait for public disclosure within local governments, but now we can finally move forward.

> Of course, there are practical issues to be addressed, such as how to provide incentives to release software, and how to identify and manage software that has been released to the public, but we are very happy to have made a step forward on an issue that has been a decade in the making.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1993712759360671763] In Japan, it has long been legally unclear whether software developed by local governments could be released as OSS. Because of this ambiguity, many local governments hesitated to publish their software out of risk aversion.

> In today’s session of the National Diet, Takahiro Anno questioned this legal interpretation and obtained a response from the Minister for Internal Affairs and Communications stating that there is no problem in doing so. As a result, local governments in Japan can now release their software as open source without concern.

> This is a major step forward for the sharing of digital public goods among Japanese local governments, and there is hope that in the future these assets can be shared from Japan with the rest of the world as well. #plurality

> In Japan, it has long been legally unclear whether software developed by local governments can be released as OSS. Because of this ambiguity, many local governments were hesitant to release software out of risk aversion.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1993716247520034932] A local government wants to help other local governments by publicly sharing software they have developed. They were hesitant because they were unclear if that was legally OK, but it was clarified that it was OK. Isn't that a good thing? What's the problem? Who's in trouble?

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1993717771096797321] (GPT5.1) Until now: the business of creating and selling similar resident information systems and application systems separately for each municipality has been established.
> From now on: If OSS created by some municipality can be horizontally deployed by other municipalities, the number of "projects to be created by full scratch every time" will decrease.
>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1993717787072823320] People in trouble:
> Large and local SIers who have profited from custom projects
> Vendors who have locked in with "This is a package exclusively for this municipality.
> These people tend to lobby negatively for OSS underwater, saying "security...", "liability...", etc.
>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1993718070372876341] I'm not saying that, I'm just presenting the GPT 5.1 answer, so any complaints about this interpretation should be directed to OpenAI...

Slogan: "New Labour, New Britain" ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Labour?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
BACKGROUND: After 18 years of the Conservative Party (Thatcher - Major), it won the election by remaking itself into a "modernized Labour Party, a centrist party".
A Rough Picture of the Policy
1. economy and finance

On the macro level, the Thatcher era [market economy] and [financial liberalization] are basically maintained (i.e., not [anti- or anti-Thatcher]). ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Labour?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Emphasis on "credible fiscal and monetary policies," including Central Bank independence and inflation targets.
2. welfare ("[From welfare to work]")
Emphasizes "work incentives" and "skill investment" [workfare-type welfare] rather than mere redistribution.
3. public services
Increase public investment in education, healthcare, etc., while introducing private sector methods (market mechanisms/outcome indicators).
4. social policy
Relatively liberal on human and minority rights (e.g., expanding LGBT rights). ([Taylor & Francis Online https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/02691720110057306?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
5. diplomacy and security
Emphasizes alliance with the U.S. and has been heavily criticized for his support of the Iraq War.
2. "New Liberal" = Third Way

A frequently mentioned ideological label for the Blair administration is ** "[Third Way]"** and the theories of sociologist [Anthony Giddens]. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Way?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Difference from old left and right
In Giddens and Blair's organization:
Old Left (Traditional Social Democracy)
Redistribution through nationalization, strong unions, and big government
Neoliberalism (Thatcher/Reagan type)
Deregulation, privatization, small government, market universal
The Third Way (New Liberal)
Accept market economy and globalization as a prerequisite
However, the state actively supports "equality of opportunity" and "social inclusion" without leaving disparity and exclusion unchecked.
Emphasizes not only "rights" but also "responsibilities (self-responsibility/responsibility to society)"

Blair himself calls it "the new socialism" (social-ism), in which individuals are interdependent and how to reconcile social solidarity and social justice with individual choice and the market. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Way?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3. what exactly is "new"?
1) [Liberals not hostile to the market].
Major revision of Clause IV, which called for "[nationalization]" of the former Labor Party Charter.

→ Weakened nationalization orientation to the phrases "[balance between market and public sector]" and "[wealth creation + social justice]". ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Labour?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
A self-portrait of a "Labor Party that can also work with business."
(2) Emphasis on "opportunity" and "ability" rather than redistribution
The program should be combined with "employment support and job training" rather than simply providing benefits to the unemployed.
Emphasis on long-term "capacity building" including education, skills investment, and child poverty reduction.
(iii) Re-emphasis on morals

He emphasized the ethic that "if you insist on rights, you must also fulfill your responsibilities," and was criticized as a "moral panic" and "moralizing politics." ([Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung Bibliothek https://library.fes.de/pdf-files/bueros/suedafrika/02824.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
4. evaluation and criticism
supportive evaluation
In the post-Thatcher political map, the Labour Party established a "middle-of-the-road line that could win elections". ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Labour?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Influence center-left parties in other countries as an eclectic model of "market + welfare" rather than [selecting an option (from two alternatives)] of conservatives and leftists.
criticism
From the left.

The reality is only "[soft neoliberalism]" and criticism that it has hollowed out social democracy. ([Dissent Magazine https://dissentmagazine.org/article/new-labour-and-the-destuction-of-social-democracy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
He pointed out that the government left inequality and excessive growth in the financial sector unchecked.
From the right.
Criticisms such as high regulatory and social spending have impeded growth.
5. summary: the blair government and the "new liberals
The Blair administration has abandoned the classic "Labor Party = anti-market and big government" image,
It is positioned as a "third way" left-of-center faction that pursues social justice while embracing the market economy.
The "new liberals" are,
While assuming a free market,
A position in which the state and community try to fill in the gaps and exclusions that would occur if left unchecked with "equality of opportunity" and "social inclusion".

[https://tse4.mm.bing.net/th/id/OIP.dFXh2AV_s4A__GoYLkwa9AHaFj?pid=Api https://www.mobygames.com/game/1835/simearth-the-living-planet/screenshots/macintosh/522019/?utm_source=chatgpt.com]
Is your recollection of those days correct?
1.[Gaia Theory] and [Daisy World].

SimEarth is a planetary simulation based on James Lovelock's Gaia Hypothesis, with Lovelock himself as an advisor & wrote the foreword to the manual. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SimEarth?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
There is a section in the manual called **"TESTING THE GAIA HYPOTHESIS - DAISYWORLD "**,
Black daisies absorb light and warm the planet.
White daisies reflect light and cool the planet.
The explanation is well written. ([Internet Archive https://archive.org/stream/Mac_SimEarth_manual/SimEarth%20manual_djvu.txt])
And in later chapters,
You'll see "dark, light, and neutral-colored daisies."
Planetary mean temperature is self-regulating through albedo (reflectance)
There is also a Daisyworld commentary called ([Internet Archive https://archive.org/stream/Mac_SimEarth_manual/SimEarth%20manual_djvu.txt])
→ My recollection of "black and white daisies to adjust temperature" is quite accurate.
2. about the monochrome Mac version

The manual clearly states that "the screen shots in the manual are from the Macintosh monochrome version and the IBM Hercules/MCGA monochrome version," indicating that there was a black and white version for the original Mac. ([Internet Archive https://archive.org/stream/Mac_SimEarth_manual/SimEarth%20manual_djvu.txt?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
How to play now?

Unfortunately, it is not currently available for official download (GOG, Steam, etc.); GOG only has a wish list of "please get it". ([GOG https://www.gog.com/wishlist/games/simearth_the_living_planet?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
So the realistic option is "emulator + older version".
A. The easiest way: Try the DOS version in your browser
If you just want to quickly remember the atmosphere:
1. search for "SimEarth My Abandonware" etc,

There is a page where you can run the DOS version as-is in your browser (internally in DOSBox). ([My Abandonware https://www.myabandonware.com/game/simearth-the-living-planet-10c?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
When the page is opened, the game starts automatically and is operated with the keyboard and mouse.
Since the copyright is grayish, we feel that we should use the archive with the awareness that we are using it for preservation purposes.
B. Play properly on your own Mac: DOSBox + DOS version
For macOS (10.15), it is practical to run the DOS version in DOSBox. ([Abandonware DOS https://www.abandonwaredos.com/abandonware-game.php?abandonware=SimEarth&gid=631&utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Rough procedure:
1. install DOSBox
Get it from the official site per "dosbox mac download".
2. prepare a disk image or folder of the DOS version of SimEarth
If you already have the actual item, such as a floppy or CD, a clean way to use it is to make an image of it.

Even if you don't own it, the DOS version is archived at so-called abandonware sites, but this is a self-responsibility zone. ([My Abandonware https://www.myabandonware.com/game/simearth-the-living-planet-10c?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3. mount and start the folder in DOSBox
Example: `mount c ~/games/simearth` → `c:` → `simearth.exe`.
The UI and content is almost identical to the Mac version of the time, and includes the Daisyworld scenario. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SimEarth?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
C. If you want to be "Mac-like": Classic Mac emulator + Mac version
I really want to do it the Mac way!" In case of:
1. classic Mac emulators such as Basilisk II / SheepShaver.
2. install images of System 7 to 9 and Mac version of SimEarth.
3. start up and reproduce the entire Mac environment from the black-and-white to 16-color era of that time.

The Mac version is called "SimClassics 2", a set of SimCity, SimEarth, and SimFarm that is archived as a disk image. ([macintoshrepository.org https://www.macintoshrepository.org/52950-simclassics-2?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
The setup here is also a bit geeky, but it comes closest to the "Mac at a relative's house" feel.
In a nutshell:
The "Gaia Theory + Black and White Daisy" game I remember is almost certainly SimEarth.
That explanation is certainly detailed in the manual.
If you just want to lightly touch it right now, it's a "browser version of a DOS emulator",
If you want to sit down and do it properly, it's either "DOSBox" or "Classic Mac Emu".
Once you have decided which route you want to play, we will write a more specific procedure focusing on that method.
